| G15: counts take a folder's totals with rows hidden | `select` `a9_4_selection_counts_each_byte_once` |
| G15: `retain_shown` skips with a selection | `tests_selection::rows_no_longer_shown_leave_the_selection`, `p_random_gestures_…`, `fixes::the_mark_goes_with_its_side` |

**W9b.** Interpretations and extensions of §1.9.12–§1.9.15 (one implementer):

1. `OpPreview` keeps per item only the dry run's status and reason (`PreviewItem`, 2 bytes), the summary, the counts,
   the warnings and the backups; `line(plan, i)` builds the item's DTO with the one builder the executed and dry-run
   items use (`folder_ops::item_dto_of`, new) and prints it with `item_line`; `line(plan, len())` is the summary line.
   The counts are W6d's lines in core (`PreviewCount { kind: Action(word) | Skipped | Failed, items, bytes }` and
   `text()`); their items add up to the dry run's `planned`. The dry run's warnings are the plan's, the batch's and the
   shadowed members' notes: `hikasa_vfs::ops::shadow_drop_warnings` (new) borrows the plan, `note_shadow_drops` is now
   its `&mut` wrapper. Measured: 2 bytes an item (100,000 items, counting allocator).
2. `SyncPreview` keeps the indices of the rows the human output shows (4 bytes a row), the batch's `OpPreview`, the
   counts and the number of emptied folders. A row's line needs its path, which `SyncPlan::rows` holds only as a node:
   `folder_sync_preview(&plan)` keeps the contract's signature and `SyncPreview::line(plan, read, i)` takes the
   comparison's `TreeRead`; `kind(plan, i)` tells a row (conflict, unresolved, overridden), an emptied folder, an item,
   the summary and the counts apart for the colours.
3. `api::vocab::parse_touch_time(text, zone)` takes the zone (the Service's clock's, `human::TimeZone`): RFC 3339 first
   (the CLI's `--time`), else `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, `YYYY-MM-DD` local; a
   local time a DST change skips is taken after the gap, a repeated one is the earlier (jiff's *compatible*).
4. `ViewKind::is_served` (new: M1's kinds and `folder_sync`) replaces `is_served_in_m1` in the IPC server, `check_open`,
   session views and the GUI; `unserved_view` names the kind for every other one. A folder-sync session opens as
   `ViewRequest::Sync` with its folder rules and `[rules.sync]`; the words of `--sync` and `folder sync --gui` apply over
   the `folder-sync` defaults' options (a view opened without a preset syncs as a new Folder Sync session would).
   `ViewOutcome::Sync`'s result carries no verdict.
5. The sync half is held by the folder view model (`FolderViewModel::sync: Option<Box<SyncViewModel>>`) instead of a
   `SyncViewModel` that wraps the tree: every tree path (columns, selection, Find, Legend, the verbs, path edits, the
   base commands, sessions and workspaces) serves both view types without delegation, and `ViewModel::scope` says
   `Scope::Sync` for a model with a sync half. Check 2 bans `#[path]` in `src/`, so the child modules of
   `folder_view.rs` are `folder_view/verbs.rs` (the verbs) and `folder_view/sync.rs` (§1.9.15's `sync_view.rs`); check 7's
   model list takes the `folder_view/` directory and `content_dialogs.rs` (Exclude, Compare Contents and its results,
   Quick Compare). `lookup(Scope::Sync, id)` falls back to the Folder Compare row of an entry both views share
   (`folder-shared`, `session`); only the `folder-sync` entries have rows of their own.
6. `PlanConfirmDialog` owns the plan and its preview (`PreviewList`) and hands them back with its answers
   (`take_answered`): the view keeps no copy of a plan while its questions are asked. For a verb without options the
   confirmation is the preview dialog (the list, *Include hidden items*); toggling the check box closes it and the view
   plans the same request again with the new value (a new confirmation follows). A verb dialog's Start hands its plan and
   questions to the view the same way; a plan without a question runs at once (W6d).
7. A verb dialog (`OpDialog`) plans at its next poll after an option change, so changes made before one poll make one
   job; an older job is cancelled and its answer dropped by a generation. A comparison changed under the dialog
   replaces Start by *Plan again*, which runs the command again on the current selection with the remembered choices.
   The choices are written to `state.dialogs` only on Start. Touch's mode words are the dialog's own (`other-side`,
   `set-to`), Rename's `mask` and `regex`; the structure and overwrite words are core's (`PathStructure::as_str`, new).
8. `CopyPrompt`/`MovePrompt` ask with a button per side that can take the items (writable, the other side has selected
   items, and for a move the source side writable too); the answer runs `CopySide`/`MoveSide` with the opposite pane as
   `CommandArg::Side` (new). Without a pane, `CopySide`/`MoveSide` take the focus side when one side alone is focused.
9. Rename of one row edits the name cell of the first selected writable side in place; Enter plans
   `RenameMask::Name` on the selected writable sides, Esc or a click elsewhere cancels, an empty or unchanged name does
   nothing; a taken name fails the item (core). More rows open the dialog, prefilled with `base_mask` of the names.
10. New Folder needs no selection (`Predicate::AnyWritable`): it goes into the current row's folder (a folder row, a
    file's parent, else the base) on the focus side when one side alone is focused, else on the remembered sides, else
    on both writable sides.
11. `Ignored` is a check of the current row's mark; it sets (or clears) the marks of every selected row; the list
    `folder_set_ignored` returns becomes the view's `rules.ignored` patch and the tab's session is changed.
12. Exclude reads its masks in a job (`folder_exclude_masks`) and on OK adds them to the view's session through the
    reopen path (a folder-sync session's folder rules too). Compare Contents counts the file pairs it reads in a job
    (`folder_selection` and the subtree of each selected folder) for its question; its method defaults to the
    remembered one, else the session's content method (none: Binary); the view's `Task::Contents` holds the refresh claim
    as an operation does, and its counts line goes to the log. Quick Compare runs `Service::quick` on the selected file
    pairs' canonical specs in one job.
13. Compare To and Open With ▸ *Text Compare*/*Folder Compare* open through `home::resolve` (`infer_view_kind`, the kind
    forced) in the view's window. Open With's items are `CommandArg::OpenWith(OpenWithItem)` (new, GUI: `TextCompare`,
    `FolderCompare`, `App(index)`), since core's `OpenTarget` has no view kinds; `AssocApp` is the submenu's last item
    (`LIST_CHILDREN`) and stays a command. Applications run in a window job (`CoreJob::Launch`); one with
    `refresh_when_finished` refreshes the selected rows' parents when it ends; a launch error is a warning notice.
14. The Synchronize preview's options start from the `folder-sync` defaults (`orphans`, `create_empty`,
    `within_archives`, `recycle`, `recycle_fallback`) with the command's preset; Run is off while nothing acts; its
    questions use the dialog's mode: Prompt asks the operation question with the counts (§1.9.14), Yes and No to All
    answer every question as core's `Confirmation` does in those modes (pressing Run is then the go-ahead).
15. The Folder Sync view plans for a (model, generation) key: the plan follows the comparison's end, every refresh and
    re-run by the key alone, and every change of the preset, an option or an override by a due flag; the plan job does
    not make the view busy (its commands stay available) but the window polls on while one is due. `RowView` gains the
    row's action and a folder's summary, read per rendered row from `SyncPlan::rows` by node (an index map) and
    `SyncPlan::folder`; a folder left alone whose rows below act shows its summary and a small mark. An override the plan
    cannot take and no row took is named by `SyncPlan::dropped_overrides` and removed, its warning the notice; one that
    names no row (`SyncPlan::unused_overrides`) is kept (both additive core fields, each path with its `switch_ignored`
    warning; corrected after the review, note 21: the first version removed both, beyond §1.9.15). Run moves the plan into the
    confirmation; a cancel or an error plans again; *Sync within archives* re-runs the comparison.
16. The waited outcome is complete when the comparison is not running and `view_verdict` is not `Incomplete`; a Run's
    code is `FolderSyncOutcome::exit_code`.
17. D-256's threshold is the constant `LONG_OPERATION` (10 s) against the time from the execute job's start to its
    outcome; an operation's, a sync's and a content compare's outcome effect is `Effect::Beep` of its window.
18. Check 7's planner rule reads every Rust file under `gui/` (tests too); `op_dialogs.rs` names no `plan_counts`.
19. G15 at the end of W9b (`docs/02`, load 3.2–7.1): the bench modes `preview` (every row shown, Select All on the left,
    Copy to Right: 100,020 items) and `sync_view` (`--sync`, Mirror to Right, then Leave Alone on one row). Sync **met**
    (plan 145 ms after the comparison, an override 234 ms, scrolling max 1.0 ms). Preview: scrolling (max 2.2 ms), PSS
    (+69 MiB) and the 2 bytes an item **met**; the first frame **not met** (1,281 ms against 1 s): the time is core's
    `folder_op_plan` (0.62 s for the plan alone on a tree with a tenth of the folders, preview and confirmation 3 ms);
    reported as found, the threshold unchanged. The W9a rows measured again: select, completion, browse met; tree max
    met and p95 not (9.28 ms), as after W9a. A Folder Sync view shows every row unless its request names a display (its
    catalogue section has no display-filter commands, §1.9.15).

*After the W9b review* (one fixer; the findings F1–F14 by the review's numbers, then the mutations that survived):

20. A sync whose view ends goes on as an operation does (§1.6.25 W6d after review): `RunningOp` carries either job
    (`RunningJob::{Op, Sync}`), `retire` keeps a running sync cancelled, it ends after its current item (no temporary
    file left), its outcome reaches the log through `sync_log_entries` with one notice naming the tab and how it ended,
    and Quit waits for it as for an operation. A waited Folder Sync view closed while its sync runs leaves `gui list` at
    once, but its waiter is answered when the sync ends, with the sync's own exit code (`Shared::take` keeps the waiter
    with the orphan; a sync still running at the end of the exit wait answers 100). After Session Settings' OK the view
    lives on: the ended sync's code becomes its last Run.
21. Overrides a plan does not use (§1.9.15, FS-004): core names them apart. `dropped_overrides`: a row could not take
    it and no row took it (a folder's override that some row below takes is used); `unused_overrides`: it names no row
    of this comparison. The view removes only dropped ones (with their `switch_ignored` warning as the notice, the
    session changed) and only from a *whole* comparison that still stands: complete (not stopped), no folder not
    scanned, no row unresolved and none left because a filter hides a side (the plan job reports it), the plan's
    (model serial, generation) the view's. Unused ones stay in the options: one notice per path and view, and the
    header's "n overrides name no row" with the paths as tooltip. A Folder Sync view scans every folder (`sync_folder_rules`),
    so its incomplete cases are a stop, a failed listing and a filter; Synchronize ▸ removes nothing.
22. The plan job of a Folder Sync view also makes the questions (`folder_confirmation`, which reads `options.toml`) and
    tells whether the comparison is whole: Run hands the job's `Confirmation` over and nothing reads a file or walks
    the items on the window's thread (the Synchronize preview's job makes its questions in the dialog's mode, a change of
    mode plans again). Run needs a plan of the current options: an edit of the options drops the ready plan at once
    (`plan_ready` also requires no plan due). Plans are keyed on (the view's model serial, the model's generation),
    the serial counting the models the view prepared, never an address. While the comparison runs and once the model
    changed under the ready plan, the rows show no action of it and Info none of its counts (`current_plan`).
23. The Synchronize preview's Run after the comparison changed shows "… the comparison changed while the sync waited;
    nothing was written. Plan again." and replaces Run by *Plan again*, which runs the Synchronize command again, as an
    operation dialog does (§1.9.12); its poll notices the change too.
24. Open With an application and the associated application (FC-062): more than ten items (`LAUNCH_ASK`) ask "Open n
    items with <application>?" first; the launch is a job of the view (the job indicator lists it, its Stop cancels
    it); the programs start one after the other, the cancel checked before each, and the first that cannot start stops
    the rest with an *error* notice naming it ("…; the n items after it were not opened"). In core, `AppLauncher::start`
    (additive, default: `run`) starts a program and returns what waits for its end; `open_with_run` without
    `wait_for_previous` starts each in turn and waits for them on threads of their own. Folders open with the system
    handler as files do (`open_associated`).
25. Compare To, Quick Compare and Open With ▸ *Text Compare*/*Folder Compare* pass the items' `Spec`s: Quick Compare's
    requests take `spec_os_string`, and a view of two items is built in-process (`infer_view_kind`, then
    `open_view_request` with the specs' exact OS strings in place of their text), since the IPC-shaped `resolve_open`
    refuses a path that is not valid UTF-8. The registry and the tab keep the specs' text (lossy, for display). A9.30's
    test makes the names with a byte that is not UTF-8 (Unix) or an unpaired surrogate (Windows) and does not run on
    macOS, where APFS cannot hold such a name. Compare To's browsed second item is parsed by the Service in the job.
26. `refresh_when_finished` keeps the paths of the rows' folders (`selected_parent_paths`) and finds them in the model
    as it is when the application ends (a folder gone is skipped).
27. A relative Copy/Move to Folder target is read with the source side's base folder as the current folder (the focus
    side, else the side that has the items, else the left; `~` the home folder); a base that is not a local folder asks
    for an absolute one. The dialog shows "Into <folder>" (or the message) under the field; Start sends the resolved
    spec, and `mru.folders` keeps it in full.
28. Compare Contents' end is a `FolderEvent::Ended { elapsed }` the window beeps for (D-256); a Run whose job fails
    sets the waited code to 100 (A9.17); a view whose bases cannot be loaded is `load_failed` before any sync outcome
    (D-23).
29. Exclude adds each mask once through `app::ops::add_masks` (unit-tested: the dialog cannot select a row a mask
    already hides). The behaviours the other surviving mutations exposed were already right; each now has a test
    (table below).
30. G15 preview, core: a side entry keeps a fingerprint of its identity (`EntryView::ident`, from `FileId`: device and
    inode where std gives them, MemoryVfs's; 0 when none; `SideRec` 72 bytes, a node 176, within M1's 256 bytes a node).
    A copy that replaces a local file decides "the same file" from the model: different fingerprints are two files; no
    identity on either side (Windows' local disks, where the identity check never applied) with bases that differ by
    `spec_key` are two files; equal fingerprints, one unknown, a followed or name-only source, a move, or a member of an
    archive ask the disk as before (`same_file`). Execution checks both stamps as before. The planner makes a row's specs
    and its item's path from its parent row's, kept while one folder's rows come (`TreeRead::spec_below`, additive),
    caches the capabilities of non-archive specs by scheme without a key string, moves the specs into the item and reads
    the time rule once per item. On the G15 tree `folder_op_plan` went from 0.77–0.86 s to 0.30–0.32 s (load 6–29); the
    plan is the same (compared on that tree without the row ids, which a parallel scan numbers as they come; the plan
    goldens and properties unchanged). `tests/perf_plan.rs` (ignored) measures it; the preview bench reports the plan
    job's own time (`plan_job_ms`). No parallel planning was needed. G15 after the review (`docs/02`, load 6.7–14.1):
    preview **met** (first frame 330.7 ms, the plan job 324.8 ms of it; scrolling max 3.04 ms; PSS +84.3 MiB); sync met
    (200.8 ms, an override 274.0 ms); select, completion and browse met; tree max met and p95 not (14.43 ms over 10
    frames while scanning, W9a's open finding). Taken again at load 3.8 (2026-11-08): p95 4.69 / max 4.97 ms over 22
    frames, met. G7 copy failed once at 1.61 × while the load rose from 5.5 to 26.6 (2026-11-05); at load 3.8 it gave
    1.41 and 1.43 ×, met (`docs/02`): its targets are absent, so the identity check never runs for it, and execution is
    unchanged.
31. A9.30 under wine: wine keeps names as UTF-8 on the Unix side and cannot create one with an unpaired surrogate
    (`ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`), while NTFS takes any UTF-16 code units through the wide calls (`OsString::from_wide`).
    The test creates its folder first; when that fails it panics unless it runs under wine (the system folder holds
    `wineboot.exe`, which Windows never has: a marker of wine itself, not the runner's `WINEPREFIX`) and under wine
    ends there with a line saying so. It runs whole on Linux and on Windows CI; macOS is out (note 25). It is not one of
    §6.6's wine-only failures (it passes under wine), but under wine it checks only that the name cannot be made: a
    limit of wine, decided after the review (the same probe as A7.6's `a7_6_names_that_are_not_unicode`).

**W9c.** Interpretations and extensions of §1.9.16–§1.9.18 and §1.9.21–§1.9.22 (one implementer):

1. Clipboard file lists (D-252). `FixedClipboard` holds a list as its content once one is placed (`files`,
   `set_files`, `file_lists`): `read_files` gives it back, `read` sees no text, as on a real clipboard. `FileClipboard`
   keeps one path a line (a Unix path's bytes, so a name that is not UTF-8 survives) and refuses a path with a line
   break; it reads `\r\n` and skips empty lines. `SystemClipboard` uses arboard's `file_list`; on Linux the D-203
   helper takes the list on its stdin (the second length is `FILES_MARK`, then each path and a NUL byte) and owns it
   until something else is copied; its test placer writes it one path a line. arboard's own Linux list canonicalizes
   the paths and leaves out those that do not exist.
2. *Show in File Manager* (D-254). The pure `host::reveal_command(platform, path)` gives the command line,
   `reveal_fallback` the folder, `file_uri` the URI: every byte but the unreserved ones and `/` percent-encoded, so a
   comma (`dbus-send`'s array separator), a space and a byte that is not UTF-8 survive. Windows passes
   `/select,"<path>"` as one raw argument (the quotes keep a path with spaces whole; `explorer.exe` exits 1 when it
   worked, so only a failed start falls back); `dbus-send --print-reply --reply-timeout=5000` waits for the file
   manager's answer, so a missing service falls back to the folder; macOS falls back when `open -R` fails. The Service
   adds `open_folder_in_file_manager` (*Open Folder in File Manager*: a folder itself, a file's folder, a member's
   archive's folder) and the pure `api::file_manager_targets`, which the window uses to enable the entries per side
   (`Ctx::explorer`). Both run in a window job (`CoreJob::Pane`); an error is a warning notice.
3. `Service::check_folder_rules` is `FolderRules::validate` (schema, masks, the offset) with the warnings the comparison
   would give: `switch_ignored` for opened archives while archives are files, `unknown_config_key` for a format id the
   registry does not know. It reads no file (the masks compile, the registry is in memory), so the dialog calls it on
   the window's thread: at each poll after an edit changed what the tabs would write, and again at OK.
4. The drop prompt (`drop_dialog.rs`) plans the copy and the move in one job, again on each change of the overwrite
   choice, and its preview switches between them (Shift at the drop shows the move first and makes *Move* the
   default): either button runs a plan the user could see, unchanged (T12). The choices are `--overwrite`'s words
   (*Fail*, *Skip*, *Replace if newer*, *Replace*), remembered in `state.dialogs.drop`. A copy is recursive with the
   default metadata. The preview lines are core's `human::vfs_op_lines` of the dry run.
5. A drop or a paste goes into the folder row under the pointer, else its nearest folder above that the side has, else
   the side's base; a read-only side (*Disable editing*, `--ro`) and a view without a comparison answer with a message.
   Paths dropped on the centre keep W4's window rule. The run is a task of the view (`Task::Transfer`, `vfs_op_execute`
   in a `VfsWrite` job): one operation at a time, Stop cancels it, a view that ends keeps it as an orphan
   (`RunningJob::Transfer`) whose outcome still reaches the log, and D-256's beep applies. Its end refreshes the folder
   it went into and, for a move, the folders of the sources that lie below a local base of the view; the notice is
   core's summary text, the log gets each failed line.
6. `Paste` goes into the current row of the side a context menu names, else of the focus side: a folder row itself, a
   file's folder, else the base; with both sides focused it says "Select a row on the side to paste into." rather than
   guess. The clipboard is read in a job: its files first, else the lines of its text that parse as specs other than
   `-` and `clipboard://` (as typed, resolved by the plan); nothing to paste is a message.
7. `Copy` and `Copy Filename` list the items in the model's tree order (`items_in_order`: folders first, the left side
   first per row), not the order of a column sort. A context menu's side restricts `Copy` to that side's items. Both
   write through the GUI's own writing clipboard (the provider of a script's `output-to:clipboard`, D-203) in a job.
   `Copy Filename` writes no line end after the last line.
8. The text-field rule (D-252). egui turns Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V into clipboard events; while no text edit has the
   keyboard (`Context::text_edit_focused`) the window turns them back into those keys for the dispatch, otherwise the
   field takes them. A focused text edit is `FocusArea::TextField` (beside `PathField` and `HomeSearch`), whose keys
   Ctrl+C/X/V/A (`is_text_edit_key`) neither dispatch nor bubble to the root, whatever command a user bound to them;
   `Ctx::folder_pane` (the window's `text_focus`, set each frame) turns Copy, Paste and Select All off in the menus too.
9. The pane menus are D-253's normative lists in `commands::pane_menu_ids` (order and separators are part of them)
   rather than the rows' `areas`; `takes_side` names the entries that carry the clicked side. The menu flag of
   `commands.toml` is the menu bar's: the context menus keep their entries (captions and shortcuts follow the file).
   *Reset Columns* (`CommandArg::ResetColumns`) puts back the default columns, widths and the tree order; it ends View ▸
   Columns too. A right-click in a Folder Sync view's centre shows the sync pane list without a side. The menus are
   built only while one is open.
10. Rows dragged (D-251) carry egui's payload `RowDrag` (the side pressed, the selection); the release over the tree
    finds the pane and the folder row; the rows must still be the selection when it lands, rows pressed in the centre
    go from the side opposite the release. Copy/Move to Folder is prefilled through `VerbOptions::into` (the folder,
    *relative*, the side the rows came from).
11. The rule tabs (D-249): `SessionTab` gains `load`, `prepare` (`TabExtras`: `format list`, the presets; read in the
    store job before the dialog opens), `check` and `error`. OK writes each changed tab's keys over what the tabs before
    it left (a fold; W4b's first-tab-only would drop the others). The tabs edit typed field sets (`ComparisonFields`,
    `ListFields`, `HandlingFields`, `MiscFields`, `SyncFields`); a field that does not parse (a tolerance that is not a
    whole number of seconds in `u32`, hours that are not a number) is the tab's message; core says the rest. Handling
    hides *Ignore folder structure* in a Folder Sync session (a sync refuses a flat comparison). The Misc tab's check box
    that gives a format its global state back removes the session's entry, so bold rows are the overrides; ids of
    formats the registry does not list stay. A matrix cell changed from a preset copies the preset's matrix into
    `custom` first. `Rules` is `Never` in text views until W11.
12. `session edit --set` names only keys the session file spells out (an existing limit): the FC-012 keys a default
    omits (`auto_scan_subfolders`, `expand_on_load`, `expand_differences_only`) cannot be compared with it, so A9.23's
    scope test takes the P0 keys it can name; the GUI writes those keys through the same `session_apply_scope`.
13. The Filters edit (D-250): one `FiltersEdit` per view (`FolderViewModel::filters_edit`), taken again from each new
    model unless the field is being edited; Enter of the view's own filter runs nothing; Esc puts it back. The text is
    parsed with case-sensitive mask options (the syntax does not depend on the case; the comparison compiles again with
    its own). The field is shown in Folder Sync views too (their catalogue has no `NameFilterEdit`, so only the focus
    command is Folder Compare's). A new filter goes through W4b's reopen path (`reopen_changed`).
14. *Add To Presets* (`PresetNameDialog`): an empty name or one in use is refused; the write is `settings_save` of
    `filters.toml` on the window's settings queue. On a `Conflict`, *Overwrite* writes with `force`, *Reload* reads the
    file again and adds the preset to what it holds now (the concurrent change is kept), *Cancel* keeps the dialog; the
    prompt's answer reaches it by `Followup::Presets`. The Name Filters tab asks the window for the prompt
    (`DialogRequest::AddToPresets`).
15. The drop prompt's help is `view-folder-compare` (§1.9.24 lists no topic of its own); the drop, the clipboard and the
    context menus are described there.
16. The window's side of the panes is `app/pane.rs` (a model file of check 7, as `drop_dialog.rs`): Copy, Copy
    Filename, Paste and the file-manager entries run in window jobs (`CoreJob::Pane`); A9.25's window test is taken
    headless instead, through the real drawing code with synthetic egui input (`ui/tests_pointer.rs` `w9c_*`: a
    right-click and its menu entry, a row dragged to the other pane, Ctrl+C from the tree and from the Filters edit, a
    file dropped on a pane), which needs no display; the `#[ignore]` window test under xvfb was not added.
17. G15 and ARCH-GUI-003 at the end of W9c (`docs/02`, release, xvfb with llvmpipe, 2026-11-08, load 5.0–8.6): every
    row **met** — tree p95 6.88 / max 6.88 ms with PSS 161.1 MiB, select (Select All 3.8 ms, Shift+Down p95 0.42 ms),
    preview (first frame 153.9 ms, +78.4 MiB), sync (58.7 ms, an override 85.9 ms), completion 157.0 ms, browse
    201.7 ms; `text_scroll` 277.2 MiB and ≥ 302 fps, `two_windows` 284.9 MiB with p95 4.02 / max 13.21 ms,
    `workspace_restore` −0.02 MiB a pending tab. The tree row's p95, W9a's open finding, met here as in the round at
    load 3.8 after the W9b review; every row is one run on a machine others load, so the GPU run stays the
    maintainer's (§6.9).
18. The pre-push run of W9c (`prepush.sh`: every CI job, wine, macOS clippy, `PROPTEST_CASES=4000`) found the drop
    property's report comparing a Windows source path through `{:?}` (its backslashes escaped, so `<root>` did not
    replace it) and, with 4,000 cases, too many cases rejected for an empty drop; the property now prints the texts as
    they are and always drops at least one entry (both mutations of its table caught again). Under wine the rest failed
    only in §6.6's five wine-only tests; every W9c test passes there.

*After the W9c review* (one fixer; the findings F1–F17 by the review's numbers, then the mutations that survived):

19. **A move never takes items from a read-only side (F1).** `FolderViewModel::move_refused` maps each source onto the
    view's bases by its path (`path_within`: components, `.` dropped, `..` taken back, a verbatim Windows prefix read as
    the plain one, names folded on Windows and macOS; a member base by its outermost archive, a snapshot by its file): a
    source that is a read-only base or lies below one makes the drop prompt *Copy*-only, *Move* off and its preview the
    reason (note 5's message, `read_only_message`). `drop_answered` checks a move again before it runs; a refusal then
    runs nothing and is the view's message. The check is by path, not by the disk: a source reached through a symbolic
    link to a read-only base is not recognised (the plan's own checks apply).
20. **Rule tabs write only their changes (F2; revises the scope path of note 11).** `apply_scope` (core, D-82) writes
    `change` sparse against the view's rules before it (`view.rules` on entry) over the defaults, or over the override it
    replaces (Pair, Type: that override's keys kept, the change written over them, sparse against the defaults): a value
    the view held on its own (an earlier *this view only* edit, its Ignored paths, its sync overrides, opened archives, a
    command line's filters, `format_overrides`) stays the view's, and a Defaults write equals `session edit --set` of the
    keys edited (`tabs::a9_23_values_the_view_holds_on_its_own_stay_out_of_the_defaults`, from each of the three). W4b's
    text tab takes the same path. A key the dialog *removes* (an optional value cleared) is not carried to the defaults
    (as `session edit --set` cannot say it either).
21. **Ctrl+V with files only, Shift+Del, the image paste (F3, F15).** `ui::clipboard_key`: egui-winit swallows a pressed
    Ctrl+V and sends `Paste` only with text (`PasteImage` with an image), so a Ctrl/Cmd+V (Windows: Shift+Insert)
    release with no paste since its press, no text field and no dialog taking keys, is Ctrl+V; a paste event sets the
    window's `paste_seen` and its release clears it (losing the keyboard clears it too); a press that reaches the window
    itself is dispatched as it is. `PasteImage` is Ctrl+V. A `Cut` with Shift held (egui-winit's Windows Shift+Del) is
    Shift+Del (Delete Permanently), else Ctrl+X. A Ctrl+V released after Ctrl is not a paste (the release carries no
    Ctrl).
22. **A drop whose place is unknown asks (F4, F8).** winit 0.30 sends no `CursorMoved` while another program holds the
    drag (X11 ignores `XdndPosition`, Windows and macOS pass none), so egui's position is the one from before the drag.
    Per window, `OsDrag` keeps when the drag began (its first frame with hovered or dropped files) and when the pointer
    last moved or pressed; a position counts only when it is as fresh as the drag, else it is discarded everywhere (the
    Home fields, the type buttons, the panes, the hover highlight). A drop on a folder view without one is
    `DropTarget::PaneAsk` → `DropOutcome::Ask`: the prompt (`DropDialog::asking`) shows *Into the current folder of:*
    per side its `paste_into` folder or why it cannot take them, the focus side first (else the side that can), and for
    one or two paths *Open as new comparison* (`OPEN_NEW`), which applies W4's window rule to the paths (two open as a
    comparison, one gives its hint); with neither side able, only that and *Cancel*. Modifiers are read in the drop's
    frame: Shift shows the move first and makes it the default (note 4), unless the move is refused. On the maintainer's
    desktop list (A9.30): a drop with the pointer still and moving, per platform.
23. **Rows dragged onto a folder carry its spec (F5).** `DropInto` gains `spec`; `VerbOptions::into` is `(Spec, Side)`;
    `OpDialog::prefill_target` keeps the spec beside the canonical text it shows, and `resolved_target` takes the spec as
    it is while the field holds that text (no trim, no new parse; edited, the text is read as typed). A folder whose spec
    `is_lossy` is refused with "Rows cannot be dropped into a folder whose name is not valid Unicode."
24. **Pasted text (F7, revises note 6).** `clipboard::pasted_paths` (core): each line, trimmed, that is an absolute local
    path or a `file://` URI with no host or `localhost` (case-insensitive scheme; `%XX` decoded; Unix keeps the bytes,
    Windows takes `file:///C:/x` as `C:\x` and needs UTF-8; the native separators since W9's close, note 36).
    Anything else, a relative path included (it named the window's current folder), is left out, and a text of none
    is "The clipboard holds no files to paste."
25. **A drop on a file row (F9).** `FolderViewModel::drop_row` gives any row's node to OS drops; `drop_into` goes up from
    a file to its folder as from a folder the side lacks. Rows dragged between the panes keep D-251's rule (a file row of
    the other pane is "outside a folder row").
26. **Menu entries as their commands (F10).** `Ctx` gains `clicked` (a pane menu's side) and `focus_side` (one side
    focused); `Predicate::CopyFromSide` (`CopySide`: items on the side acted on, its other side writable),
    `MoveFromSide` (`MoveSide`: that and the side itself writable), `PasteSide` (`Paste`: a pane, a finished comparison,
    nothing running, the side acted on writable; with neither side known it stays on and asks for a row, note 6) and
    `AnyWritable` with a clicked side needing that side (New Folder, which now presets the clicked side and refuses it
    when read-only). `AppCore::enabled_inv` checks an invocation that carries `CommandArg::Side` with it (a menu entry, a
    prompt's follow-up). The pane goldens changed for the orphan's right pane and the read-only side.
27. **Tab errors (F11).** `SessionSettingsDialog::tab_caption` marks a tab that holds an error `(!)` (drawn in the error
    colour); `DialogModel::button_tip` (new, default none) gives OK's disabled tip "The <tab> tab holds an error:
    <message>".
28. **The clipboard's writes and helpers (F12, F13).** `OrderedClipboard` (core) wraps the GUI's writing provider: a
    command takes a `Ticket` on the window's thread, its job writes `in_turn`; a ticket older than the last one taken
    writes nothing, writes never interleave, plain provider calls (a script's `output-to:clipboard`, Info's Copy) take
    theirs when they write. The Linux helper's `Child` is waited for on a thread of its own (`host::reap`). arboard 3.7
    has no other format API and bypassing it needs an X11/Wayland client of our own (new crates, D-258), so on Linux
    `host::local_uri_paths` fixes only what it reads wrong (`file://localhost/p` → `/p`, another host's file and any other
    relative path left out); the rest is documented (docs/04 FC-080, `view-folder-compare`): a list placed is canonicalized
    by arboard (a link's target, missing items left out), a list read drops a URI that is not UTF-8 decoded.
29. **File-manager commands (F14).** `reveal_command(platform, path, cwd)` starts in `launch_dir` (Windows
    `%SystemRoot%\System32`, else `C:\Windows\System32`; elsewhere the home folder when absolute, else `/`), never the
    item's folder. On Windows the item must exist and `explorer_path` must give a form explorer selects (`\\?\C:\…` →
    `C:\…`, `\\?\UNC\s\h\…` → `\\s\h\…`; a device or volume path has none), else the folder opens; a started
    explorer counts as shown whatever its exit code. *Open Folder in File Manager* keeps `open::that_detached` (the
    process's own folder; revised by note 34).
30. **The keyboard's context menu (F16).** Shift+F10 or the Menu key, while the tree has the keyboard or nothing has it
    (a binding of the key wins first), opens the menu of the focus pane (the centre's with both sides focused; a sync
    view's pane) for the current row, anchored at that row (`egui::Popup::open_id` with `at_position`).
31. **The Filters edit (F17).** `FiltersEdit::check` parses without touching the text; Enter shows the canonical text and
    records the MRU only once the view takes the filter (a busy view keeps the text as typed); *Add To Presets* saves the
    canonical text and leaves the field; a new model replaces the text only when it is not being edited (also when the
    view had no filter). A reopen (Session Settings' OK) builds a new view, whose field starts from its filter
    (revised by note 35).
32. **The review's survivors (F6).** Tests now catch M1–M4, M6, M7, M9, M13, M16, M18–M22, M25 and M29 (table below).
    Equivalent: M5 (`drop_into` without `present_on`: `TreeRead::spec` is `None` for a side without the item, so the walk
    goes up the same; `fixes::f6_a_drop_on_a_folder_the_side_lacks_goes_up` pins the behaviour), M8 (`clipboard_paths`
    keeping the root: the root is no row, so no selection holds it), M14 (dispatch without the
    text-field guard: `dispatch_keys`' own `is_text_edit_key` rule keeps the keys), M30 (`focus_area` without
    `TextField`: `text_focus` already keeps the clipboard events for the field).

33. **Gates after the review** (`docs/02`, release, xvfb with llvmpipe, 2026-11-08, load 5.0–9.1 falling from 18): the
    rows the fixes touch, each **met** on its second run — tree p95 7.37 / max 7.37 ms with PSS 153.6 MiB, select (Select
    All 4.1 ms, Shift+Down p95 0.54 ms), `two_windows` 259.0 MiB with p95 2.86 / max 8.26 ms. The first runs, started
    while the machine was still loaded by other sessions, had the tree's p95 at 8.0 ms over two frames and one
    `two_windows` frame of 23.15 ms; both are recorded. The other rows are untouched by the fixes (note 17 stands).

*At W9's close* (two decisions taken after the fixer, and what the close's pre-push run found; revise notes 24, 29 and 31):

34. **Open Folder in File Manager starts in the fixed folder (revises note 29).** `AppLauncher` gains `open_folder(path)`
    (default: `open_associated`, so a launcher that does not know it behaves as before); `Service::open_folder_in_file_manager`
    and *Show in File Manager*'s fallback call it, and `RecordingLauncher` records `Recorded::OpenFolder`. `open` 5.4.5
    takes no folder to start in, so `SystemLauncher::open_folder` runs the pure `host::open_folder_command(platform,
    path, cwd)` (Windows `explorer.exe "<path>"` after `explorer_path`, macOS `open <path>`, Linux and the other Unix
    systems `xdg-open <path>`) in `launch_dir`, as `reveal_command` is run. A started explorer counts as opened; elsewhere
    an opener that ends with an error within `OPEN_CHECK` (250 ms, `open`'s own check) is the error, one still running
    then has handed the folder on and is waited for on a thread of its own (never a zombie). When the program cannot
    start, `open::commands` of the platform are tried in turn, each in the same folder. No new crate. Tests: the pure
    builder per platform with `launch_dir` (`launcher::the_folder_opener_of_each_platform_starts_in_the_fixed_folder`)
    and the records of the Service and the GUI (`OpenFolder`); no test starts a program.
35. **A reopen keeps the Filters edit (revises note 31).** `AppCore::reopen` (Session Settings' OK, and the filter's own
    Enter) hands the old view's `FiltersEdit` to the new one (`FolderViewModel::keep_filters_edit`): the text being
    typed and its message stay, nothing is pushed to `mru.name_filters` (only Enter of the field records), and the
    field then follows the new model as after any run (note 31): edited, it keeps its text and compares with the new
    view's filter (Esc shows it); not edited, it shows the new filter. Test:
    `tests_rule_tabs::a_reopen_keeps_the_filters_edit`.
36. **A pasted `file://` URI on Windows has Windows' separators (revises note 24).** The W9 close's pre-push run under
    wine found `file:///C:/x` pasted as `C:/x`: the same file typed as `C:\x` gave a second, differently spelled source
    in the drop prompt (`tests_pane_fixes::f7_…`). `path_of_uri` now turns every `/` into `\` (never part of a Windows
    name); `clipboard_files::pasted_text_names_only_local_absolute_paths` compares the paths as text on Windows, since
    `PathBuf` equality takes `/` and `\` as the same separator.
