#### 1.10.25 Dependencies and architecture test (D-291)

- **No new crate.** `regex` and `fancy-regex` are reached through `hikasa_formats::Pattern` (already in the workspace,
  M1); `ropey`, `encoding_rs`, `memchr`, `rayon` are already `hikasa-text` dependencies; `rustix` is already
  `hikasa-vfs`'s (the `access` call is in `src/local/unix.rs`). `LoadStamp`'s CRC-32 comes from the VFS primitive
  (VFS-020; additive `hikasa_vfs::crc32_bytes(&[u8]) -> u32` beside `crc32_reader`), so `hikasa-text` gains no
  dependency. `hikasa-folder` keeps `hikasa-formats` (D-180) for `template`. `Cargo.lock` gains no package; `cargo deny`
  passes without new exceptions; `docs/02` gains no line.
- **Check 3.** Every manifest unchanged; the table is unchanged.
- **Check 2.** In `core/hikasa-text/src` and `core/hikasa-diff/src`: no `std::fs`, `std::process`, `std::net`, no clock
  (`Instant::now`, `SystemTime::now`): typing time comes from the adapter (`GroupHint::Typing`), the save program runs
  through the injected `ProcessRunner` (D-39). `save/source.rs` reads only through `&dyn Vfs`.
- **Check 7.** Nothing in `cli/` or `gui/` names `hikasa_diff::align`, `align_traced`, `hikasa_text::compare(`,
  `compare_with_limits`, `compare_live`, `save_content`, `plan_save`, `execute_save`, `execute_with`,
  `Pattern::compile`, `template::` or `hikasa_formats::encode`: adapters reach them through the Service or the pure
  entry points of §1.10.23 (`EditableDocument`, `LiveComparison`, `Finder`, `nav`, `details`, `transform`, `commands`);
  `gui/` computes no text edit (no `rope` mutation, no `ropey::Rope::insert`/`remove`). Each new rule has a
  planted-violation self-test. No `unsafe`.

#### 1.10.26 Gate G8 and budgets (D-271)

Measured at the end of W10a (edit rows) and W10c (all rows), release build, idle machine, inputs generated by the test
(the G1 pair `c_pair(1,000,000, 0x5EED_0001)` and its rules: c-cpp, Auto → Standard); harness
`core/hikasa-text/tests/gates.rs` (`g8_*`, `#[ignore]`), median of 20 edits at seeded random places unless stated,
figures in `docs/02`.

| Item | Scenario | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| G8 type | one character typed into a **same** line; `note_edit`, then `recompare_job(..).run` + `install` | recompare: every one of the 20 < 50 ms; `note_edit` < 1 ms |
| G8 changed | one character into a changed line (inside a change cluster) | < 50 ms each |
| G8 lines | Enter in the middle of a line; deleting a line; pasting 100 lines | < 50 ms each |
| G8 copy | Copy Section to Right of a 10-line section | < 50 ms |
| G8 undo | 1,000 single-character edits at random places (each `note_edit`, a recompare after every 50), then 1,000 `undo` calls each with `note_edit`, then one recompare | the 1,000 undos + their `note_edit`s + the recompare < 1 s; the result equals the original comparison (P-EDIT-1 on the gate input) |
| G8 memory | the edits and undos above | RSS growth after the 1,000 edits and their recompares < 10 MiB; live heap growth (counting allocator, CI on 100,000 lines with the same per-edit bound: `core/hikasa-text/tests/edit_memory.rs`) < 10 MiB per 1,000 edits |
| G8 worst (reported) | one character in the common prefix (the segment's root re-runs) | reported; ≤ G1's align phase on the pair |
| G8 save | save of the 48 MB left side with 1,000 edited lines, `MemoryVfs` and local disk | ≤ 1.5 × `vfs cp` of the same file + 0.1 s; peak heap ≤ 8 MiB + the edited text |
| G8 find | `Finder::all` of a plain word and of a regex `\b\w+_17\b` over the 1M-line side | < 150 ms; < 400 ms |
| G8 find files | `text find` of a word over G7's 10,000 small files, warm | ≤ 1 s; output order identical with 1 and 8 threads |
| Cancel | a recompare, a save, a find in files cancelled midway | returns ≤ 100 ms (G4) |
| G1, G5 | the M1 gates on the block line table and the chunked rows | unchanged (G1 < 3 s; G5 `row` < 200 ns, `FilteredView::get` < 200 ns, `inline` p99 < 50 µs) |

A failure is reported with its figures (docs/17 §7.1), never met by relaxing a rule. W11 re-measures the typing latency
in the window and ARCH-GUI-003 with an edited document and 1,000 undo steps (plan W11).

#### 1.10.29 W10 notes (implementation)

*To be written by each part*, as §1.9.25: every point where the implementation interpreted or extended the text above,
numbered per part, with the mutations each property and integration test was checked by (§6.10 rules).

**W10a.** Interpretations and extensions of §1.10.2–§1.10.11 and the W10a share of §1.10.22–§1.10.26:

1. INV-ALIGN-8 held on every engine before any change: every imara-diff call and Standard's stages renumber the range
   densely in first-occurrence order (`DenseRemap`), so no engine needed a fix; P-ALIGN-REN passes 20,000 cases and the
   M1 goldens are untouched. P-ALIGN-REN also compares the derivations (and `align_traced` = `align`).
2. A block is one `Arc<[u8]>`: `n` relative starts (the first slot, always 0, holds the *marked* flag), `n` terminator
   codes, and in a block an edit touched `n` generations and `n` file lines; `first_byte` is `u32` (texts are below
   4 GiB) and `first_line` stays empty while uniform. Headers and prefix sums take 0.07 bytes a line. The last block may
   hold fewer than 128 lines (as a load builds it); `uniform` also needs the last block ≤ 512 lines.
3. Positions: after a terminated last line (and in an empty document) one empty line holds positions
   (`EditableDocument::position_lines()`) but is never a table line, so the table always equals a fresh build of the
   text. A lone CR line meeting a following empty LF line is joined into one CRLF line by the edit (the span is widened),
   exactly as a load reads those bytes.
4. Every request becomes changes that replace bytes inside spans of whole physical lines; a `Batch` turns its ranges
   into changes last-first, each just before it is applied. Lines whose content and terminator are unchanged at a
   span's start or end keep their marks (Enter at a line start marks only the new line), and the deltas are trimmed to
   the changed lines. `EditOutcome` gains `deltas` (each change's own delta; `delta` is their union).
5. `TextDocument::marks` returns `LineMarks { generation, orig }`; `EditableDocument::mark` gives
   Original/Edited/SavedEdit; `saved()` records a save for W10b. Undo restores a change's marks when the change was made
   after the last save; otherwise the restored lines take the undo's generation and no file line.
6. Typing coalesces inserts at the caret within 1,000 ms; the *word start* rule applies to inserts only (Backspace
   through a word stays one step); a step never merges across the save point. `with_limits` (hidden) lowers the D-43
   limits for the `TooLarge` tests.
7. Anchors are a parameter of `align_anchored` / `align_traced` (with `auto`: *Auto* decided per segment), not an
   `AlignOptions` field, so `AlignOptions` stays `Copy` (M1 API); `CompareInput` gains `anchors` instead. Runs never
   merge across a pair's boundary: INV-ALIGN-9 wins over INV-ALIGN-5 there (INV-ALIGN-5 holds inside each segment;
   `Alignment::check_invariants_anchored`). With *Auto* and anchors the reported algorithm is Standard when any
   segment ran Standard, else Histogram. Dropped anchors give one `anchor_dropped` warning each
   (`DiffWarningCode::AnchorDropped`, `WarningCode::AnchorDropped`).
8. `PairScorer` gains `begin_gap()` and `spent()` (defaults); the text scorer empties its profile windows per gap, so a
   gap's scorer units depend on that gap alone (only once the scorer's budget runs out does this differ from M1).
   `TraceNode` gains `scorer`, `refusals`, `candidates`, `band`, `band_margin`; `SegmentTrace` gains `pair` and `work`;
   `WorkTotals` gains `scorer`; `exhausted` covers the order-dependent refusals only (work budget, fallback, the total
   closeness cap, a scorer that ran out). `hikasa_diff::canonical_runs` (additive) canonicalizes concatenated runs.
9. Rows are a chunk store (`compare/store.rs`): chunks of at most 1,024 rows whose lines are relative to per-chunk
   bases; a splice rebuilds the touched chunks (merging below 256 rows), later chunks change bases.
   `TextComparison` derives `Clone` (documents and chunks shared) and gains `anchors()`, `provisional()`.
10. The provisional splice works on a window of the touched rows widened to whole sections, so sections, class runs
    and statistics are re-derived over that window only; runs are cut at the window's edges. A section of N changed
    rows costs O(N) per `note_edit` (a pair that differs everywhere); the G1 pair's sections are small.
11. `note_edit` also gives `current()` a snapshot of the edited document, so the comparison's documents follow the
    panes and `copy_rows(current(), …)` reads live text; a pending row's inline difference is the plain inline diff of
    the live lines, all important. An anchor that loses every line is dropped and reported by
    `LiveComparison::take_warnings` (the comparison itself equals a fresh compare); `set_anchors` makes the next
    recompare full. `install` of a result older than the installed one changes nothing (`Replayed` with the pending
    count). A recompare's `bytes_identical` is the base's while no edit or anchor change came since, else false.
12. The incremental path covers one segment (no anchors) aligned by Standard or Patience; anchored comparisons,
    Histogram, Myers, Unaligned, a recorded exhaustion or refusal and the T6 thresholds take the full compare (the same
    result). Condition 4 keeps upper bounds: old totals plus every re-run's work, re-extension steps and remap growth,
    never subtracting replaced work (a later full compare resets them).
13. Checkpoints are `(line, state)` pairs that move with edits: every 64 lines at load, made again inside re-keyed
    spans and at their ends. Re-keying grows a span line by line while the old and new end states differ (absorbing an
    adjacent span first), instead of stopping only at checkpoints.
14. A re-keyed span is alignment-dirty whole unless every key (and weight, with Standard) equals the old line's: in a
    span whose line count changed no inner boundary is fixed. Condition 1 checks the boundary pairs after the prefix and
    before the suffix by key.
15. Condition 2 extended: when the recorded chain holds every candidate (`TraceNode::candidates`), candidates may leave
    (their line changed or their key stopped being unique) and join (a key became unique in the window), as long as
    the new set still increases on both sides; the chain is then the new set. Otherwise any such change fails.
16. Condition 3 is exact: Standard records the unique pairs whose start or end displacement lies within
    `WINDOW_BAND` = 256 lines of the skew (`band`); every other pair is farther than `band_margin`, which certified
    edits wear down by their largest cumulative shift (several dirty spans: the largest shift before and after any
    line, both sides). Band pairs are checked one by one; with an all-candidate chain a pair entering or leaving the
    window joins or leaves the chain. Patience has no window. Re-extension reuses whole old blocks whose anchors,
    surroundings and bounds are unchanged; other pairs are compared by key (equal pairs inside an old block on the same
    diagonal with clean lines are known equal).
17. The session share (W10a): `TextCompareRequest::anchors`; one vocabulary parser `api::vocab::parse_anchor` for
    `<L>:<R>` and `left|right:<a>[-<b>]` (`parse_align`, `parse_isolate`, `parse_anchors` take one form each; side
    words through `parse_side`). A line beyond a document is `invalid_input` (exit 100) after loading and before
    comparing, for pairs and isolated ranges alike (the CLI never clips). JSON `anchors` is always present (`[]`),
    right after `rules`, 1-based half-open ranges, `kind` `pair`/`isolate`, inapplicable fields `null`. `--gui` with

21. G8 (§1.10.26) is not fully met; the figures are in docs/02 (a failure is reported, never relaxed). The review fix
    (notes 22–39) re-measured every row: see note 39.

*W10a review fix* (findings F1–F12 and G8 of the independent review; the owner's rule: the option with more
functionality and performance):

22. **F1.** Under *Auto* the recompare finds the segment's new common prefix and suffix (`Inc::new_prefix`/`new_suffix`:
    steps of known-equal pairs on the old `Equal` runs' diagonals between re-keyed lines, key comparisons elsewhere,
    O(change)) and takes the full compare when the engine they give is not the recorded one (test
    `auto_is_decided_again_from_the_new_prefix_and_suffix`).
23. **F2.** FF-024 `or_line_one` makes line 0's key depend on its line number: with such an item (additive
    `CompiledGrammar::has_line_one`) an edit reaching line 0 grows the span at line 0 until it holds the old and the
    new line 0 (`LineMap::touch_line_zero`). P-EDIT-2's generator gains such a format (unimportant or not, 0–2 next
    lines); test `edits_at_the_first_line_rekey_the_old_and_new_line_zero`.
24. **G8 a, edge deltas.** A node whose ranges map to its old ones and hold no dirty line is copied; otherwise it is
    certified on its new ranges: new prefix and suffix as in note 22, the middle non-empty on both sides, and the
    lines that move between the stripped ends and the middle (the new middle against the mapped old one; a clean
    line's old line is in the old middle exactly when its new line is in that interval) count for condition 2 as
    removed or inserted lines. A new gap is mapped to the one old gap it overlaps (meeting intervals; an empty one
    holds its point) and that gap's recorded child is processed on the new ranges, unless new blocks split that old gap
    (several new gaps meet it: each part is re-run; processing the child on each part was found inexact by a
    4,000-case run, test `a_split_old_gap_is_never_processed_in_parts`); a gap over several old gaps is re-run (mapping it to the largest recorded child among them was tried and was inexact on a nested case, persisted
    in `props_incremental_more.txt`). A reused block's region now reaches the next anchor (the pair where its forward
    extension stopped may lie in the next block's backward extension), and the per-node state of the window check is
    cleared before each node: two inexactnesses of the W10a code found by the new nested and batch properties.
25. **G8 b, exact window.** `TraceNode` loses `slack`, `band`, `band_margin` (and `WINDOW_BAND`) and gains `diag`, the
    node's unique pairs (in the window or not, trivial keys left out) as maximal diagonal runs `(x, y, len)`: every
    unique pair whose left line is in a run's range lies on its diagonal. Membership depends on a pair's diagonal
    relative to the middle's start and on the middles' lengths, so each run is cut into the pieces that stay clean
    inside the new middle and each piece is decided before and after (`Inc::window`): with an all-candidate chain a
    piece that leaves takes its chain pairs out and one that enters adds its unique pairs (equal ids on the diagonal,
    counted unique in the new middle); otherwise any change fails. The new runs are the pieces plus one run for each
    pair that became unique (cutting a run it falls in), consecutive runs of one diagonal merged. The mutations of the
    worn band (review M06, M07) have no code left to mutate.
26. **G8 c, interned ids.** `live::ids`: per side every line's interned key id (`u32`) in chunked `Arc` blocks of at
    most 1,024 (`IdLines::spliced` rebuilds only the chunks a span touches); one `IdTable`: per id the key's 64-bit hash
    (the full run's ids renumbered in hash order, looked up by binary search; ids made by edits in an overlay map),
    occurrences per side capped at `u16::MAX`, a trivial bit. A recompare interns each new key: an id it already gave,
    the id of a removed line with the same key, or a live id with the same hash whose key a clean line holding it
    shows equal (one walk of the ids finds a line for every such check, then that line is re-keyed); else a new id.
    Its changes (`TableDelta`) are applied at `install` (`LiveKeys::settle`, in place unless a job shares the table).
    Equality is one id comparison; condition 2 counts keys by a walk of the middle's ids that stops when every key is
    complete (cap reached, or every occurrence the table counts found; dirty and moved lines are counted at once and
    skipped). A key absent from a whole side after the edit is unique nowhere: it is not walked, and its old chain pair
    (it has a removed or moved-out line) is found in the chain by that line. The 16-bit fingerprints and the
    4,096-verification limit are gone. Deviation from the review's design: no stored positions (they would cost 8–12
    bytes a key and a remap per install); the walks and the shortcuts above find what positions would give. Memory:
    §1.10.2's table is amended (4 bytes a line a side, 12 a distinct key; the G1 pair's live data is 24.4 MiB).
27. **G8 d, shared derivation and the Step 3 splice.** The live derivation (`ids::LiveTrace`) keeps each recorded node
    in an `Arc` with a lazy offset: a clean subtree is copied by cloning its `Arc`s with a new offset (O(nodes), no
    chain copied); a node on the dirty path is read moved (`LiveNode::absolute`). `LiveKeys::derivation()` (hidden)
    materializes a `Derivation`. Step 3 compares the new runs with the old ones moved: the stretches that differ, and
    the runs holding re-keyed lines (a line re-keyed with an equal key is only re-classified), build their rows (the
    old row's classification where it pairs the same clean lines), which replace the old rows of the stretch, with
    sections, class runs and statistics changed by difference over the whole sections around it
    (`splice::replace_window`, shared with the provisional splice); every other row chunk is shared.
28. **T6, the work guard.** The incremental path counts its work (`Inc::spend`: lines re-run, lines moved between a
    middle and its ends, one unit per 128 ids walked); past 65,536 units and an eighth of both documents' lines the
    full compare is cheaper and runs instead (the same result; `PathCounters::fallback`). `PathCounters::rerun_lines`
    (additive) counts the re-run lines.
29. **F3.** The G8 memory row reads the current `VmRSS` before and after the 1,000 edits and their recompares (and
    resets `VmHWM` for the phase's peak); the undo row compares runs, every row, sections, statistics and warnings.
30. **F6.** P-EDIT-2 compares the inline differences of every row (`common::canonical_json_all`) and the anchors
    against `AnchorModel`, which tracks line identities instead of reusing `move_anchors`. New properties:
    `p_edit_2_nested_documents` (the review's nested generator, skews 0, 3, 20, 40, 100, 300, duplicate, move and
    paste edits), `p_edit_2_batch_requests`, `p_edit_2_out_of_order_installs`; in hikasa-diff
    `p_node_locality_every_recorded_node_aligns_alone_as_in_the_full_run` (`props_locality.rs`) and
    `p_align_ren_random_permutations_of_large_alphabets` (shuffled alphabets up to 400 symbols, small, large and huge
    ids; the table scorer reads symbols modulo 8). The path sweep adds nested cases so that condition 3 fails too.
31. **F7.** `copy_rows` takes the target pane's insert terminator (`insert_eol`, D-290) for a terminator it has to add.
32. **F8.** `LiveComparison::inline` computes a pending pair's differences from the live lines whatever its state
    (`None` when they are equal). `LiveComparison::check_invariants` (hidden) checks every invariant of `current()`
    but INV-TC-8 on pending rows, which keep their old state until the recompare classifies them
    (`TextComparison::check_invariants_except`).
33. **F9.** `undo`/`redo` return `None` on a blocked pane, `try_undo`/`try_redo` give `EditError::Blocked`,
    `can_undo`/`can_redo` are false while blocked (test `undo_and_redo_respect_the_editability`).
34. **F10.** Each section keeps its rows by class (`SectionCounts`, checked by INV-TC-3); an edit strictly inside a
    section of more than 4,096 rows (two unrelated files are one section) changes it by difference
    (`splice::replace_inside`: kind, importance, line ranges, statistics, class runs joined at the edges) instead of
    re-deriving it; an edit at such a section's first or last rows still re-derives it. Gate
    `g8_note_edit_in_one_huge_section`, test `edits_inside_a_huge_section_keep_it_exact`.
35. **F11.** `EditableDocument::new` re-wraps a document whose artificial breaks are not its own limit's
    (`TextDocument::normalize_wrap`: a check of every line's length, a rebuild only when needed), so undo restores the
    loaded table.
36. **F12.** Check 2's text engine rules and check 7 resolve renamed imports, crate and type aliases and globs as the
    banned tokens do (`resolved_code`); a glob of an engine crate in an adapter is a violation; planted self-tests for
    each. **Windows read-only volumes:** `Vfs::writable` reads only the DOS `R` attribute on Windows: the volume's
    read-only flag needs `GetVolumeInformationW` (D-99: no `unsafe`, and `std` does not expose it), so a read-only
    volume is left to the save, which fails with the OS error (§1.10.7's table is read accordingly).
37. Found by 4,000-case runs: P-ARCH-2's model comparison took a root that the archive refuses at planning (a target
    below a link member, rule 5: never followed) for a different outcome than the model's failed first step (it
    follows the dangling link): the model now takes a failed root with nothing below it run as one outcome; the minimal
    case is the test `a_copy_below_a_link_member_fails_like_the_model`. `align_traced` (and `align_anchored`) now warn
    `closeness_ignored` for Myers with closeness when no segment reached the engine, as `align` does.
38. The review's survivors are killed by tests (table below): typing never merges across the save point
    (`typing_never_merges_across_the_save_point`), EROFS reads as read-only (unit test of the errno table), anchors move
    with their lines (`anchors_move_with_their_lines` and the anchor oracle), `bytes_identical` holds only until an
    edit (`bytes_identical_holds_only_until_an_edit`).
39. G8 after the fix: see docs/02 (W10a review fix table).
40. **G8 follow-up, the gap plan** (`Inc::gap_plan`, edge deltas). A certified node's old gaps are mapped to the new
    numbering. A new gap that is exactly one old gap mapped, met by no other new gap and without dirty lines keeps its
    runs and subtree. Otherwise each recorded child goes to the one new gap that overlaps its old gap most (lines of
    both sides; ties to the first) and is processed there on the new ranges (`Inc::node`: its prefix, suffix and middle
    found again; the lines new to its middle are inserted and those that left it removed for condition 2); each other
    part is re-run. So a child is processed on one gap at most whatever new blocks split or merge the old gaps; this
    replaces the review fix's rule that re-ran every part of a split old gap (the cause of the Enter, delete, copy and
    paste fallbacks: a 1–100-line shift moved a piece across a window edge, split a gap, and its 377,000-line child
    re-ran). The child is processed only when its moved lines plus twice its chain cost less than six times the gap's
    lines (performance only). A gap given no child that equals one of an old child's own gaps (mapped exactly, same
    lengths, no dirty line) keeps that gap's runs and recorded grandchild (`Inc::child_gap`): the engine processed
    exactly those lines as one range.
41. **Moved lines by whole-document counts** (`Inc::new_chain`). The lines moved out of or into a middle are no longer
    all counted by a walk. With an all-candidate chain and a key that has no dirty line: a moved-out line whose key has
    no other line on its side (count 1) or none on the other side takes at most its own pair out, which the chain's
    clipping to the new middle does (a pair with a line outside the new middle is no candidate there); a moved-in line
    whose key is absent from the other side is unique nowhere; a key with one line on each side whose two lines both
    moved in is a new unique pair, joined by id (one line alone is counted). Every other moved line is counted like a
    dirty line. Caps are `2 + known new lines` per side (deciding `was` and `is`); a key with two known new lines on a
    side (not unique now) and two known old lines on a side (not unique before) is not counted at all.
42. **The window's entering pairs** (`Inc::window`): a pair of a key with one line on each side in the whole documents
    joins the chain without a count; a key with two or more entering pairs has two lines in the middle on each side and
    is not unique; the others are counted. The leaving pairs are filtered by one merge (both lists ascend).
43. **Walks.** `count_ids` and `intern`'s walk compare up to 32 wanted ids with blocks of 16 line ids at a time
    (`Targets`; a bit test per id beyond 32), and an id leaves the set once complete; `IdView::delta_bits` marks the ids
    whose counts this recompare changes (set after the removals and after the interning), so other lookups skip the
    map; id maps hash with one multiplication (`IdMap`; the ids are the recompare's own numbers). The old chain is
    mapped in one pass (`SideView::ascending`) and `TraceNode::absolute` runs once per node.
44. **Re-runs on interned ids** (`Inc::align_ids`). Without line weights a re-run part gives the engine its interned
    ids renumbered densely left then right in first-occurrence order, which is the input `intern_pair` builds from the
    keys (INV-ALIGN-8), so no line is keyed. With closeness a first run uses a scorer that only notes the lines it is
    asked (scoring 0); those lines are keyed and a second run scores them, and a line asked by the second run that the
    first did not note fails the path (`Fail::Full`). With line weights the keys are rebuilt as before
    (`Inc::align_keys`).
45. **T6 weights**: a moved line costs 1/16 unit, a re-run line on ids 1/8, a walked id 1/128 (a re-run with keys stays
    1). No edit of the G8 rows takes the fallback now (24 of 80 before).
46. **Tests.** `p_edit_2_nested_paste_shifts` (P-EDIT-2 on nested documents where half the edits shift everything after
    them by exactly 100 lines: the same 100-line block pasted again, a copy of 100 lines of the document, or 100 lines
    removed) joins the nested property; the other nested seeds draw the same edits as before. Mutations: the table after the
    review fix's mutations below. `props_incremental`
    passed 10,000 release cases (12 tests) and the other text and diff properties 4,000.
47. **Left open.** The tokenizer start states shared by `Arc` (the first `note_edit` after a compare copies them: 1.2–2.3
    ms under load, 0.14 ms shared) collide with W11a's start-state splice and are left to that merge. Two of the 20
    paste places re-run 205,000–257,000 lines of a split child's other parts (worst 53–63 ms). `g4_cancel_w10c`'s
    recompare is now incremental (16 ms), so that row no longer cancels a full compare. Figures: docs/02 ("G8
    follow-up").

mutations above were checked: a run whose scorer ran out not counted as exhausted; condition 3 bounded by the net
change only; boundaries inside spans whose line count changed treated as fixed; a span stopping at the end of a document
before absorbing an adjacent one.

**W10b.** Interpretations and extensions of §1.10.12–§1.10.17, §1.10.22 and the W10b share of §1.10.23–§1.10.28 (the
owner's rule where the text leaves a choice: the option with more functionality and performance). The part was built in
four slices (formats and Ignored; conversions and CLI-003; the save core; the Service and the CLI), each on the previous
one.

*Formats per pane and Ignored lines (§1.10.16, §1.10.17)*

1. `CompareInput` gains `right_format: Option<Arc<CompiledFormat>>` and `ignored: IgnoredLines`; a right format equal
   to the left one (the same `Arc`, or the same id and name) counts as `None`. `TextComparison` keeps the right side's
   format, compiled rules and identity flag; `format()` stays the left one; `right_format()`, `format_of(side)`,
   `ignored()`, `section_ignored(id)` are additive.
2. Each side is keyed, weighted, tokenized and classified with its own format; elements are looked up by name
   (`RuleSet::new` per side). *Auto* gives Histogram when either side resolves to it, then D-36's size check (the
   anchored per-segment *Auto* too). Sections are one per row only when both formats are `lines_independent`. The
   identity fast path is decided per side; the raw-equality pass is skipped only when both sides took it, and
   `used_identity_path()` is true only then. In inline classification a side whose rules are all important passes no
   spans.
3. The live path stays exact and incremental with per-side formats: the recompare re-keys each side with its own keyer
   (the hash-collision check of `intern` and the per-side `or_line_one` rule included); weights count when the engine
   is Standard and either side has weights. P-EDIT-2 gives the right side its own format in a quarter of its cases
   (`per_side_formats_and_ignored_lines_stay_incremental` shows the incremental path taken).
4. `IgnoredLines { left, right: RangeSet }` (sorted, merged; serialized as a list of ranges); core clips lines beyond a
   document and never fails. Rows carry the flag in bit 4 of `PackedRow` (still 12 bytes); `Row::ignored` is serialized
   only when true. The flag is set on every row touching a marked line, *same* rows included (the colour class
   `Ignored`).
5. *Counts as same*: the row-state counts still describe the alignment; `important_rows` and `unimportant_rows` leave
   ignored rows out, so the verdict and exit code treat them as same; `TextStats::ignored_rows` counts every ignored
   row. A section whose rows are all ignored is in neither `sections`, `important_sections` nor D-18's counts; a partly
   ignored section counts whole, its importance taken from its other rows. `identities_hold` keeps the exact
   identities when nothing is ignored and becomes bounds otherwise.
6. Sections stay alignment-based; `SectionCounts` gains an ignored count; section navigation skips all-ignored sections
   both ways; class runs are split by the flag and ignored runs are in the *same* display category; `ThumbCell::IGNORED`
   (additive) is set with `SAME` on ignored differing rows.
7. Marks follow edits (`RangeSet::move_through`): range ends move as line boundaries; lines inserted exactly at a
   range's start or end stay outside it; a change that replaces a range's last line puts its new lines inside (Enter
   inside an ignored block keeps both halves ignored); a range that loses every line goes. The test oracle
   (`IgnoredModel`) keeps one mark per line.
8. `LiveComparison::ignored()`/`set_ignored()`: the provisional splice moves the marks per delta and re-flags its
   window; `set_ignored` re-derives by difference (`TextComparison::reignore`: the lines whose mark changed give rows,
   the rows windows widened to whole sections and joined within 4,096 rows; above an eighth of the rows everything),
   needs no recompare and bumps the generation. The recompare job carries the live marks; the incremental build moves
   the base's marks through the log, flags the rebuilt rows, then applies the job's; `install` of a replayed result
   re-applies the live marks.
9. `hikasa_text::ignored_check(doc, lines)` is the CRC-32 of the marked lines' text, each followed by `\n`
   (terminators and BOM left out, so a line-ending or encoding change keeps the marks); `None` when a marked line is
   beyond the document. Sessions store it as 8 lowercase hex digits; a value that is not hex never matches.
10. `TextCompareRequest` gains `formats`, `ignored` and `ignored_check: Pair<Option<u32>>`; a side without its own
    format takes D-15's format of the pair; `format` beside a side's own is `invalid_input` (exit 100);
    `format_mismatch` is dropped when a side has its own; each document is loaded with its side's format and the live
    view takes each pane's edit options from it. Per-side formats also accept *Everything Else* (reason `fallback`). A
    side whose saved check no longer matches drops its marks with `ignored_lines_dropped` (naming that side's file); a
    side without a check whose lines go beyond the file is `invalid_input`. `TextCompareResponse` gains
    `right_format` and `ignored_check`; `TextCompareRequest::with_ignored` puts flag marks on top per side and clears
    that side's check.
11. The `[specs]` keys are written only when set (existing session files and goldens unchanged), filled by
    `session_for_view`, read by `view_of` and `session run`; a session `format` together with a side's own becomes the
    other side's format; `session edit --set` reaches them; Swap Sides exchanges them; auto-saved sessions keep them.
12. CLI: `--left-format`/`--right-format` are text rule flags; `--ignored` joins the shared anchor flags (`text
    compare`, `report text`, `session run`; folder and sync sessions refuse it), its words parsed by
    `api::vocab::parse_ignored`. On `session run` and `report text --session` it replaces the session's marks of each
    side it names; `--format` there clears the session's per-side formats. `--gui` refuses `--ignored` and per-side
    formats (`OpenOptions` has neither; W11 may add them).
13. Reports: an ignored row reads as same (side-by-side and interleaved marks blank, no tones; HTML class `ign`, XML
    `ignored="true"`); patches give ignored rows importance *none* and leave out a cluster of ignored rows only, while a
    hunk with any other difference writes every row.
14. JSON: `right_format` only when the sides' formats differ; `ignored: {left, right}` (1-based half-open) always,
    right after `anchors`; rows' and sections' `ignored` only when true (the section key is an extension);
    `stats.ignored_rows` always.

*Conversions (§1.10.15, first half)*

15. Conversions work on physical lines: a `lines` range is a range of table lines, clipped; every physical line it
    touches converts whole (CPL pieces never split a rule); `TransformOutcome::lines` counts physical lines.
16. Display columns are the editor's (`edit::words::column`): a tab to the next multiple of `tab_size` (0 counts as 1),
    wide and fullwidth characters 2 columns (ambiguous ones 1), combining marks and controls 0, others 1, counted from
    the physical line's start.
17. `LeadingSpacesToTabs`: the leading blanks are spaces and tabs (an NBSP ends them); spaces before a tab that do not
    reach a stop stay (`"  \t"` unchanged); a blank-only line converts. `TrimTrailing` uses Unicode `White_Space`
    (`char::is_whitespace`; U+200B is not one). A line trimmed to empty with LF right after a lone-CR line gives `\r\n`,
    read as one CRLF line as a load would (W10a note 3); the count includes it.
18. A content conversion is one `Batch { keep_eols: true }` with one edit per run of consecutive changed physical lines;
    `LineEndings(e)` is one `SetEols` over the range's terminated lines (a last line without terminator keeps none;
    `None`/`Artificial` do nothing). When it covers every terminated line it sets `insert_eol` even when no terminator
    changes (`lines` 0, request present); `SetEols`'s whole-document test became `start == 0 && end ≥ terminated
    lines`, and an empty range that changes only the insert terminator is a step without byte change. A range
    conversion of line endings also takes the neighbours that would otherwise join a converted line into one CRLF line
    (to `Cr`: the empty LF lines after it; to `Lf`: a lone-CR line before an empty line) and counts them.
19. `SetEols` changes only the runs whose terminator differs, each as a minimal change, so a line already of the target
    kind keeps its marks and bytes (W10a's single change marked every line between, which a save would have
    re-encoded). A `Batch` of two or more edits and a `SetEols` of two or more runs are applied as one change with
    holes (`Change::holes`): one table splice whatever the number of edits (1,000,000 lines, every second line trimmed:
    18.0 s → 0.21 s, its undo 18.0 s → 0.15 s). An old line no hole starts inside or removes bytes from keeps its marks;
    the inverse change carries mirrored holes; `EditOutcome::deltas` holds one covering delta for such a step.
20. P-EDIT-1's scripts include `transform` requests (2 of 11 draws, whole or on a range, tab sizes 1, 2, 4, 8). P-CONVERT
    compares every conversion with an independent line-by-line reference of §1.10.15's table, the count included, and
    checks that exactly the changed lines are marked *Edited*.

*CLI-003 (§1.10.22)*

21. The last of `--edit`, `--sync`, `--fv` wins; `--edit` takes one or more specs (none: `invalid_input`); the pure
    `ResolvedOpen::requests(wait)` builds one `OpenView` per spec, sent in order; with `--wait` every view is awaited
    and the highest exit code reported (the first view's on a tie); `GuiOpenReport::views` (additive) lists them.
22. `--savetarget` is kept as typed by the parser (not UTF-8: `invalid_input`); `resolve_open` makes it absolute and
    canonical through the pure `api::save_target_spec(raw, &SpecContext)` (Windows: drive upper-cased, `/` → `\`, `..`
    folded, `\\?\` and `\\?\UNC\` verbatim; Unix keeps `..`); `-` and `clipboard://` are `invalid_input`; the target need
    not exist. `check_open` validates a Text Edit view's forced format and encoding before the GUI is contacted;
    `hikasa-gui --edit a` exits 100 naming `text_edit` until W11.
23. `LiveOptions::from_open(&OpenOptions)` (pure) maps `--ro*` (a Text Edit view's file is side 1), `save_target` and
    `no_backups`; `ViewOutcome::for_text_edit(loaded)` gives `NoVerdict` (0) or `LoadFailed` (100). `--edit` and
    `--savetarget` are view switches: with an `@script` they warn `switch_ignored` like the other view switches.

*The save core (§1.10.12–§1.10.14)*

24. `Action::Write` runs with full durability and `replace_link = false` and never creates parents. A target that is
    not a regular file at execution (a link included; planning resolved links) fails `invalid_target` "is not a
    regular file"; an item without `replaces` whose target appeared fails "changed since the plan was made" (the
    absent-target check lives in the runner, `needs_absent_target` being false). Without a backup the writer keeps the
    mode (D-158); with one, the replaced file's Unix mode is set again after the commit, and a failure there renames the
    backup back. `crc32_update(crc, bytes)` is the streamed form of `crc32_bytes`.
25. `hikasa_core::confirm::Ask` (additive) is the object-safe face of a question machine (`question`, `answer`,
    `remaining`); W6's `Confirmation` and the save's machine implement it and the CLI driver takes `&mut dyn Ask`.
26. `hikasa_formats::Encoder` writes `?` (`SUBSTITUTE`) for an unmappable character and counts it (no WHATWG encoding
    has a distinct substitute byte; `?` maps everywhere, through the ASCII state in ISO-2022-JP); a stateful encoding
    keeps its state across pieces; UTF-16 and UTF-32 are encoded by Hikasa. `unmappable_in` returns 0-based char
    indexes and short-circuits for UTF-8/16/32, GB18030 and ASCII text.
27. `LoadStamp`'s CRC covers the raw bytes read (before an External conversion), updated per chunk of ≤ 1 MiB; `mtime`
    comes from the stat before the read; an archive member has its own stat and Hikasa's CRC; `from_bytes` and
    `from_text` give no stamp. G1 measured before/after: unchanged (within noise).
28. The Ctrl-Z tail: the document records the format's `ctrl_z_eof`; the source is cut at the first 0x1A when the flag
    is on and the encoding is ASCII-compatible, as the load does, and the tail is written back as a `Source` piece, also
    for a whole re-encode while the source is verified; not when the source changed or there is none.
29. `EditableDocument`'s save state: location = the origin spec when `can_save_in_place`; splice source = that spec and
    its stamp (a converted or truncated document is not spliceable); with CPL the artificial lines of the document as
    loaded or last saved (`Arc<[u32]>`, empty otherwise) and the original line count, rebuilt by `new` and by a save of
    the current generation. `saved(stamp)` is an in-place save, `saved_to(&SavedFile)` the general form: at the same
    generation marks are rebased and the target becomes the splice source; at a later one (edited after the plan) the
    document stays modified and the next save is a whole re-encode (`NoSource`); Save As moves the location.
30. **After a `--savetarget` save the splice source is the file just written** (the rebased `orig` indexes point into
    it), while the document's location stays its own. §1.10.14 said the document keeps its own location *as the splice
    source*; that cannot hold once `orig` is rebased, and splicing from the target keeps every unchanged line
    byte-exact.
31. Save options: `apply_save_options` is a pure call before `plan_save` (which takes `&EditableDocument`); it touches
    the physical lines holding an *Edited* piece, Trim Trailing then Leading Spaces to Tabs composed per line into one
    `Batch` (one undo step); the document records (generation, lines) for `SaveContentSummary::pre_save`.
32. `SourceMap::scan`: one scan per item in 1 MiB steps (cancel and `reading` progress per step), `u32` line starts,
    length and CRC; a source of 4 GiB or more has no map (whole re-encode); its physical line count is checked against
    the original lines minus the artificial ones, a mismatch giving `NoSource`. A physical line is spliced only when
    its first piece's `orig` starts a source physical line, its pieces keep consecutive `orig`, and it lies beyond the
    last spliced line; other lines are encoded, consecutive ones together in 1 MiB pieces; a non-increasing `orig`
    would make a whole re-encode (never seen by P-SAVE: a save never seeks back).
33. W10a's `edit/apply.rs` matches a change's unchanged prefix and suffix in whole physical lines, so the pieces of a
    wrapped line keep their marks together (no change without CPL). P-SAVE found it: deleting a wrapped line before one
    with an equal first piece kept `orig` on part of the remaining line, which was re-encoded and lost its malformed
    bytes.
34. Re-encode reasons: `EncodingChanged`; `NoSource` (no source, converted or truncated, no map, a line-count mismatch,
    an older generation, an External save); `SourceChanged`; `Stateful` (ISO-2022-JP with any encoded line).
    `save_reencoded` is warned only when the document has a splice source. `LossyRewritten` counts encoded physical
    lines holding U+FFFD in a document whose load replaced bytes.
35. Targets: the save target, else the location, else an item error `invalid_input` "Save As needs a target". Link
    chains (≤ 40 hops) are followed relative to the link's folder, `via_link` naming the spec asked; a non-regular file
    is `invalid_target`; a second item on the same resolved target is skipped `duplicate_target`. DOS `R` or
    `writable == Some(false)` asks `ReadOnlyTarget`; on an archive member `Some(false)` is `permission_denied`.
36. `ChangedOnDisk` applies when the resolved target is the resolved splice source: the source is read and CRC'd
    whenever the save splices or its stat differs from the stamp; same bytes with a new time give `source_touched` and
    no question; a vanished target asks, Yes creating it by a whole re-encode; a changed source with another target is a
    `SourceChanged` re-encode without question. `ReplaceExisting` is asked when the target exists and is neither the
    splice source nor the location (Save As, `--savetarget` the first time).
37. `OverwriteBackup` follows W6, with the one-generation rule: a backup the document's last save made that still holds
    that file's stamp is replaced without asking (`SavedFile::backup`). Archive members: one archive backup per
    outermost file per plan (`BackupNames::assign` on that file, `rel = None`) whenever a member is written.
38. `SaveConfirmation` has no operation question; `NoToAll` declines every asking item; `SavePolicy` drops
    `ReadOnlyTarget` (`confirm_read_only`) and `OverwriteBackup` (`confirm_overwrite_newer`, as W6 asks a backup over a
    file). `finish`: declined items become `skip declined` without backup, archive backups no item needs any more go,
    `unmappable_replaced`/`lossy_line_rewritten` are added for items answered Yes, and the plan is marked `confirmed`
    (`plan_save` sets it when nothing asks; `execute_save` fails the asking items of an unconfirmed plan).
    `UnmappablePolicy::Refuse` is an item error naming the count and the first character (U+XXXX, line, column);
    `Replace` warns and asks nothing.
39. `SaveSource` reads the splice source sequentially once: `Source` ranges in ≤ 1 MiB steps, the bytes between pieces
    read and CRC'd too (returning `Interrupted` after such a step so the ops pump checks the cancel token at least every
    1 MiB), then the rest; length and CRC are compared with the stamp at the end and a mismatch fails the item before
    the commit. It refuses an item whose document changed generation, and a plan read back from JSON (contents are not
    serialized).
40. Additive beyond the text: `SaveReport::saved` (the new stamps: content bytes, mtime from a stat after the write, the
    streamed CRC), `SaveItem::mode`/`generation`, `SavePlan::confirmed`, `SaveRequest::conversion`, the `SaveIssue`
    facts `Reencoded` and `SourceTouched`; the plan's options carry `Preserve::NONE`. The External save conversion runs
    at planning (`plan_save_with` and `SaveEnv` with the injected runner): the whole text encoded (BOM included) is
    `%s`, the program's output one `Encoded` piece; without a runner the item is `unsupported`. `TextError::Save`
    exists for callers; core reports items through the `OpReport`.

*The Service and the CLI (§1.10.13–§1.10.15, §1.10.23, §1.10.24)*

41. `text_save_plan(docs, job) -> Result<SavePlan, ApiError>` (and `_on(vfs, …)`) checks every side with
    `api::ensure_editable` first (a blocked side refuses the whole call, A10.6), then plans on the router with the
    Service's temporary folder and runner. `text_save_execute -> Result<SaveReport, ApiError>` errs only on a panic;
    `api::apply_save_report` calls `saved_to` for each done item and `api::save_exit_code` is 0 when every item is done
    or skipped.
42. `Service::save_confirmation(&plan, SaveAnswers) -> SaveDriver` wraps `SaveConfirmation` with `[file_operations]`'s
    policy; `SaveAnswers` answer whole classes: `--force` *changed on disk*, `--unmappable replace` *unmappable*,
    `--yes`/`--confirm yes-to-all` the other four, `--confirm no-to-all` declines every asking item. `refusal()` is W6's
    no-terminal refusal naming the counts and the flags.
43. `backup_policy_for_save(no_backups)` returns `Result<Option<BackupPolicy>, ApiError>` (§1.10.23 said `Option`): a
    relative or empty `[backups] folder` with `naming = "folder"` is refused as W6's copies refuse it;
    `backup_policy_for_save_with(Option<bool>)` serves `--backup`/`--no-backup`. W6's policy code is shared, unchanged.
44. `LiveTextView` gains `stamps` (each pane's `load_stamp`) and `save_options(side)`; `text_compare_live` resolves
    `LiveOptions::save_target` (an archive member may be one) and sets it on the **right** document (D-275);
    `Service::live_save_request(view, side)` builds the request (in place or to the target, backups unless
    `--nobackups`, unmappable asked, the side format's External save). `ApiOp::TextSave`/`TextConvert`: every error is
    exit 100.
45. `text convert` in the Service is `text_convert_plan`, `text_convert_confirmation` (none for stdout or when nothing
    is written), `text_convert_dry_run`, `text_convert_execute(plan, out, job)`, and the one call `text_convert(req,
    out, job)`; the contract's signature gains the `out` sink for the stdout target. Files load as `text compare`
    loads them (standard input captured); a refused request (no conversion flag, several files to stdout or with
    `--output`, an unknown label or format, a tab size outside 1–32) is `ok: false` with nothing written; a file that
    cannot be loaded fails its item only.
46. Convert refuses a file with §1.10.7's words (an `EditBlocked` report): `Binary`, `Converted`, `Truncated`,
    `ArchiveReadOnly`; a read-only file is no block there but the plan's `ReadOnlyTarget` question. Its documents have
    no CPL limit, so `--lines` counts the file's lines. `converted_lines` counts the physical lines holding an edited
    piece after every conversion (every line when the encoding changes); each conversion's count is its
    `TransformOutcome::lines`; `bom` counts 0. Without `--bom`/`--no-bom` the BOM stays when the written encoding has
    one; `--bom` with an encoding without one fails the file.
47. `no_change` (nothing converted, same encoding and BOM): the file is not in the save plan and never rewritten; the
    JSON `plan` still has one item per file (a synthetic `skip` item; a file refused before planning a failed `write`
    item).
48. The stdout target makes the file's in-place plan (no backup) and streams its content from `SaveSource` into the
    sink: exactly the bytes an in-place save would write, the source CRC-checked, nothing written. Stdout asks nothing:
    unmappable characters are refused, *changed on disk* fails unless `--force`, lossy lines warn; `--json` with stdout
    needs `--dry-run`; human lines go to stderr.
49. Without a terminal open questions refuse the whole command before anything is written (exit 100, counts and flags
    named), which is how "a read-only one without `--yes` fails" is read; `--confirm no-to-all` skips the asking files
    and writes the others. `--unmappable` defaults to `refuse` without a terminal and `ask` with one. Accepted beyond
    the synopsis: `--confirm`, `--stdin-name`, `-o`, `-y`, the line-ending words `unix`/`windows`/`mac`.
50. `hikasa.text_convert.v1` follows §1.10.24; `encoding`, `bom`, `line_endings` are `null` for a file not loaded;
    `PlanItemJson` is `SavePlanItemDto` (W3's fields plus `backup` — a member's archive backup —, `expect`, `via_link`,
    `encoding`, `bom`, `bytes`, `spliced_bytes`, `encoded_lines`), shared with W10c's `text_find`. `SCHEMAS` is 42 after
    W10b (W10c's `text_find` makes 43).
51. Help: `text-convert` after `text-compare`; `index`, `cli`, `exit-codes` and `json-output` (42 schemas, the save
    warnings) updated; `docs/reference/commands.md` needed no change.
52. Platforms (A10.32): the save and convert tests run a non-UTF-8 file name on Linux; the Windows drive, UNC and `\\?\`
    spellings of Save As and `--savetarget` targets are pure tables run everywhere; the new test binaries pass under
    wine. A10.17's Text Edit `--savetarget` case uses a pane document until W10c's `text_edit_open` exists.

*Found by the gate*

53. P-EDIT-2 at 4,000 release cases (seed 8157550749541230652, a mixed pair under Standard with skew 3, none of W10b's
    per-side formats or ignored lines; the new generator's draws reached it) found an installed comparison unequal to a
    fresh compare, latent since W10a's G8 d: when a diagonal run enters a certified Standard node's window, `window()`
    counts its entering pairs with `count_ids`, one entry per pair, and the walk skipped every known line for every
    entry, so two or more pairs of one key (`def` three times a side on the entering diagonal) each counted only their
    own line, looked unique and joined the chain as anchors; the gap between the new blocks then re-ran on the wrong
    frame. A known line is now skipped only for the entry that knows it. The regular test
    `pairs_of_one_key_entering_the_window_are_counted_together` (14 × 18 lines, two edits in one recompare, the
    incremental path asserted) fails without the fix; P-EDIT-2 at 4,000 and 10,000 release cases is green.

*Review fixes (the independent review of 925e3e5..893d2b1, findings F1–F8; the owner's rule decided each)*

54. **`no_change` skips only `--in-place` (F1).** A file the conversions leave unchanged is still converted output:
    stdout gets its bytes as they are (a file through the in-place plan's full splice, CRC-checked; standard input and
    the clipboard, which have no file, read back verbatim from their capture, malformed bytes included), and
    `--output` plans a full write (the copy) with its `ReplaceExisting` question, creating a missing file. Such items
    are `done` with `converted_lines` 0. Before, stdout and `--output` got nothing (`f > f.new && mv` emptied a file).
55. **A save keeps the file it replaces (F2; revises §1.10.13's `Exec` line and note 24).** `Action::Write` opens its
    writer with `Vfs::open_save` (additive; default `open_write`). On a local regular file the writer writes **in
    place** when a rename would lose what belongs to the file and the file can be written: another hard link (nlink >
    1), an owner other than the effective user, a folder this process cannot write (`access(W_OK)`) or one that
    refuses the temporary file (`EACCES`), a group or a POSIX ACL the new file cannot take (`fchown`, `fsetxattr` of
    `system.posix_acl_*` failing). Otherwise it renames as before, after the temporary file took the owner and group
    where permitted and every extended attribute the process may set (`user.*`, `security.*` with the SELinux label,
    `trusted.*` when privileged, the POSIX ACLs as `system.posix_acl_access`/`_default`), and on Windows the hidden,
    system and archive attributes (`OpenOptionsExt::attributes`). Attributes other than ACLs are best effort.
56. **The in-place protocol (F2).** The content is spooled into a private file (`.hikasa-save-*`, mode 0600) in the
    file's folder, else the system temporary folder; nothing touches the file before `commit`. The backup is then a
    **copy** made just before the commit (never a rename: the inode, links, owner and attributes stay with the saved
    file); without a backup the writer makes and syncs a private copy of its own. `commit` looks at the file a last
    time (identity, size and time as at the open; else `changed since the plan was made`), truncates it, copies the
    spool in 1 MiB steps and syncs. A failure after the file was opened writes the old content back into the same inode
    from the copy, syncs it, gives the old time back and fails the item with "…; the file was restored from its backup
    <path>" or "…from a copy of its old content"; when the write-back fails too, "the file's old content is kept as
    <path> (<why>)" and the copy stays. Cancellation is checked up to the commit, as for the rename. The mode, owner,
    links and attributes are never touched. Cost: the spool and, without a backup, the copy (about twice the I/O of a
    rename). A crash inside the copy leaves the spool or copy on disk for the user (no automatic recovery).
57. **A read-only folder and the API (F2).** A writable file in a folder that takes no new file saves in place, with no
    backup or a backup in a writable folder; a backup that would go into the read-only folder fails the item before
    anything is written (`permission_denied` naming the backup). Additive: `Vfs::open_save(spec, opts, keep:
    Option<&Spec>)` (`keep`: the backup, used as the restore copy), `AtomicWrite::in_place()` (default false),
    `MemoryVfs::save_in_place(path)` (a test hook); W3/W6 copies keep `open_write`. The workspace's `rustix` gains
    `process` (for `geteuid`, a feature the GUI's dependencies already compile; check 3 keeps feature sets in
    `[workspace.dependencies]`) and is named in `local/unix.rs` and, for its Linux xattr test, `tests/ops_write.rs`.
    The fallback spool goes where `tempfile` puts it (core reads no environment, check 2), and the save's fault
    injection keeps its per-thread state in a mutex (no `thread_local!` in core).
58. **What a save does not keep (F2).** Windows: hard links (stable std cannot read the link count, and the VFS has no
    `unsafe`), so a hard-linked file in a writable folder is split; the file's own ACL (the new file inherits the
    folder's), its owner, alternate data streams (`Zone.Identifier` included) and the not-indexed, compressed and
    encrypted attributes. Unix rename path: `chattr`/`chflags` flags, macOS ACLs (not xattrs), the birth time. The
    outer file of an archive rebuild still takes the temporary file and rename (that path serves W3/W5 copies too).
    The safety copy without a backup in a read-only folder goes to the system temporary folder (tmpfs on many hosts).
59. **A pane takes its writability from its save target (F3).** `text_compare_live` resolves `--savetarget` before it
    builds the panes and gives the right pane's §1.10.7 facts (`writable`, archive member, location) from the target:
    a version-control tool's read-only temporary right file with a writable working copy as target is editable and
    saves there; a read-only target makes the pane read-only. Before, the pane was `ReadOnlyLocation` and
    `ensure_editable` refused the save.
60. **`text convert` streams its conversions (F4; revises note 45–46's "converted documents").** Convert no longer
    edits its documents (no Batch strings, no undo inverse, no `Encoded` copy of the file): `hikasa_text::save` gains
    `ConvertSpec { steps, lines, tab_size }`, `convert_counts(doc, spec, ctl)` (each step's
    `TransformOutcome::lines`, the changed lines, the result's lines and terminators, one pass without encoding),
    `converted_content(doc, map, spec, reencode, ctl)` (the plan's pass: the `SaveContent` of the converted text, its
    pieces `[Bom], Converted(ConvertStream)`) and `SaveRequest::transform` (additive). The stages emulate the editor
    exactly: each conversion is a stage over the lines the stages before made (so `--lines` counts as `transform`
    does), a content stage joins a lone-CR line and an empty LF line a trim made into one CRLF line and drops an emptied
    last line without terminator, a line-ending stage takes `transform`'s neighbours (to `Lf` the lone-CR run before
    the range, to `Cr` the empty LF lines after it). A line no stage touched is spliced from the source; the others are
    encoded in steps of at most 1 MiB, through one encoder for a whole re-encode; an ISO-2022-JP file with an encoded
    line, a changed encoding, a changed source or no source is a whole re-encode, as `save_content` decides.
    `SaveSource`'s reader makes a `Converted` piece's pieces as it streams them. The plan pass and the execution make
    the pieces twice (plus the count pass): CPU for memory. `TextConvertPlan::documents()` are the loaded documents
    with the encoding and BOM written. P-CONVERT-STREAM (`convert_stream.rs`, 256 cases; 60,000 green) compares the
    bytes, counts, issues, splice and the file a plan writes with the editor's `transform` steps and `save_content`.
61. **Memory of `text convert` (F4).** Release, 51,000,000 bytes, 1,000,000 lines, peak RSS under the 8 GiB scope
    (`getrusage` of the process): `--trim-trailing --in-place` 414.4 → 119.9 MiB, to stdout 414.6 → 126.5 MiB,
    `--spaces-to-tabs --line-endings crlf --in-place` 437.4 → 119.8 MiB, `--encoding utf-16le --in-place` 178.4 →
    120.0 MiB, nothing to change to stdout 120.0 → 127.1 MiB (it wrote nothing before, note 54); 120 MiB is the loaded
    document (the load's own peak). The bytes written are those of before. docs/02 has the row.
62. **What the encoder cannot write is never written silently (F5).** `maps_everything` no longer names GB18030 (the
    WHATWG encoder has no bytes for U+E5E5) and `unmappable_in` finds U+E5E5 there; ISO-2022-JP's half-width
    katakana U+FF61–U+FF9F, which the WHATWG encoder writes as full-width ones, are unmappable: `unmappable_in` lists
    them and the `Encoder` writes `?` and counts them. The save counts the encoder's replacements too: the
    `Unmappable` count is the larger of the scan's and the encoder's, so `UnmappablePolicy` decides every `?` (a
    question, a refusal, or `--unmappable replace`), also if a table missed one.
63. **An archive member written over keeps its place and header (F6; revises §1.5.10's "New or changed members" row
    and D-276).** The overlay item records the base node it replaces (`replaces`), and the rebuild writes it at that
    record's place (`Fate::Replace`): tar keeps the header and extension blocks (uid, gid, uname, gname, mode, type,
    PAX records but `size`, `mtime` and a link's), zip the central record's name bytes and UTF-8 flag, made-by host,
    external attributes as they were (0o600 stays 0o600), comment and the owner and Unicode fields 0x7875, 0x7855,
    0x756e, 0x7075, 0x6375; the data, size, CRC, method and time are the new member's (the time of the write, the
    clock's now, as for a new member). Other members stay byte for byte; shadowed older records go with it (warning as
    before); a tar hard link to it keeps the old content; a sparse member and items that bring older records go last.
64. **Standard output holds 64 MiB (F7).** `text convert` to stdout holds the bytes until the source's check at the end
    of its read when the result is at most `STDOUT_HELD` (64 MiB): a file that changed since the plan writes nothing
    (exit 100). A larger result is written as it is made, and a change found at the end leaves the bytes written so
    far (exit 100); help and docs/12 say so.
65. **`--in-place` refuses what is not a regular file before reading it (F8).** Each file is `stat`ed (links followed)
    before the load; a FIFO, a device or a folder fails its item `invalid_target` "is not a regular file", so a FIFO
    without a writer never blocks the command. Stdout and `--output` still read a pipe as its content (process
    substitution), blocking until a writer comes as any reader does.
66. **Tests of the review.** The review's save probe is P-SAVE-2 (`save_intra_line.rs`, 256 cases; 20,000 green):
    random edits inside and across lines, `SetEols`, encoding changes, undo and redo across saves of one document,
    with the Ctrl-Z tail (kept across an encoding change), GB18030's U+E5E5 and ISO-2022-JP's half-width katakana
    (encoding_rs is the oracle of what is unmappable: `Unmappable` asked exactly then, until a save wrote `?` for one,
    whose line is then spliced as written). Each mutation the review left alive has a test now (the table below):
    `a10_16_core_a_member_of_a_read_only_archive_fails_at_planning`, the time case of the one-generation rule in
    `a10_15_core_every_question_class`, `a10_14_a_source_that_grew_or_keeps_its_crc_is_changed` (a Save As of a grown
    source; four bytes forged onto the source keep its CRC-32, so only the length tells),
    `standard_output_refuses_a_file_changed_since_its_load_unless_forced` (the file replaced while its load reads it,
    Unix), `the_check_of_marked_lines_is_pinned` (literal CRCs), `a_format_per_pane_from_the_request`'s
    `format_mismatch` assertions, `a10_19_the_bom_stays_unless_asked_and_its_change_is_written`, and
    `a10_15_core_what_the_encoder_cannot_write_is_asked` (also a literal U+FFFD, no `LossyRewritten`). P-SAVE at
    20,000 cases found its own oracle too strict: an edit that leaves a line equal to the source line it replaced may
    keep that line's `orig` (the bytes are the same), so its `Stateful` expectation now follows the document's marks.
67. **G8 memory runs alone (the review's G8 finding).** The memory row is `g8_memory`, a test of its own run in a
    process of its own (`-- --ignored --exact g8_memory`, or nextest); `g8_undo` keeps the undo row. Run after the
    other gates in one process, the row measured the allocator's retention of their memory (24.2 MiB from a 400 MiB
    start). Alone, the old row gave 10.8 MiB (10.0 with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1`) against a live heap growth of 3.69 MiB
    per 1,000 edits: the undo row's oracle, a copy of the original comparison, kept a second comparison alive after the
    first recompare. Without it: growth −9.6 MiB over the 1,000 edits (the first recompare frees the initial compare's
    result) and 0.0 MiB from the first recompare on, also with one Rayon thread; the test prints both. The bound stays
    10 MiB; no allocator trim (which would need `unsafe`) or buffer reuse was needed.
