Not caught at first, and fixed: the GIF walk mutation at the descriptor's packed byte (P-DECODE's seeds had no
animation; an animated GIF is now a seed and the mutation moved to the sub-block walk, which every cut reaches); the
y-anchoring of the checkerboard (bands of 64 rows start on even cells; a tile at row 12 is now checked); the bytes
asked first (the first mutation never called the closure).

G11, engine rows (`core/hikasa-picture/tests/gates.rs`, release, `MemoryMax=8G`, desktop with 16 threads and 61 GiB,
load average 6–8 from other agents; table in docs/02): statistics of two 24 MP pictures differing in 1 % of the pixels
12.3 ms; full renders 38.9 (tolerance), 27.2 (range), 32.3 (blend), 20.7 (left pane), 43.9 ms (tolerance with the
checkerboard) (< 0.5 s each); a new offset on two 12 MP pictures median 7.6 ms, worst 8.6 ms (< 60 ms); decode of a
24 MP PNG 140 ms (< 1 s); cancel of the diff and of a render 0.1 and 4.6 ms (≤ 100 ms). All met.

**W12 review fixes.** Findings of the adversarial review of W12a and W12b (F1–F5) and its mutation survivors:

1. *F1, build output.* Criterion's output of a bench run with a relative `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` had been committed under
   `core/hikasa-vfs/target/`; it is removed and `.gitignore` ignores `target/` at any depth.
2. *F2, reads past the end.* `HexDocument::read` returns `Ok(0)` for an offset at or past the end and for an empty
   buffer, for every load (an in-memory document panicked on a slice out of range).
3. *F5, pseudo-files (HX-009).* A reported size of at most `StreamOptions::UNRELIABLE_SIZE_MAX` (4,096 bytes; the rule
   of `compare_sources` §2.20 step 2) is not trusted by the hex document either: an input loaded in memory is read
   to its end and its length is the bytes read; a paged load (a member of another back-end, or a local file when
   `unlocked_max` is below its reported size) measures its length by reading to the end through its handle and is
   never mapped. Both read at most `max(unlocked_max, 4096)` bytes; more is `too_large` (`VfsError::TooLarge`), never
   a cut document. The stamp stays the reported (length, mtime), so an unchanged pseudo-file stays unchanged.
   `/proc/cpuinfo` against `/proc/version` was two empty documents (`binary_same`) and is now `binary_different` in
   every mode, as `quick --binary` says (`verdict.rs`: a fake back-end reporting 0 and 4,096 bytes, and procfs on
   Linux).
4. *F4, GIF frames (D-337).* `image`'s GIF decoder reports the *logical screen* as the picture's size and decodes a
   first frame that does not match it into a buffer of its own (`frame width × height × 4` bytes), so a 755 KB file
   with a 1 × 1 screen and a 32,000² frame cost 4 GB and decoded `Ok 1x1`. `decode_image` now walks the GIF's image
   descriptors (`frames::gif_largest_frame`, the walk of the frame count) before creating the decoder and refuses
   any frame above `max_pixels` (`TooLarge { pixels: Some(frame) }`; any frame, not only the first one decoded, so
   the rule holds if frames are ever decoded). The allocation budget is no longer `max_pixels · 16 + 64 MiB` for the
   decode: that stays the budget while the header is read, then `decoder.set_limits` gives `pixels · 16 + 4 ·
   largest GIF frame + 64 MiB` (16 bytes a pixel: RGBA of 32-bit floats, or an 8-bit picture and its intermediate
   copies). The other containers with several images decode one image whose size `dimensions()` reports: APNG
   decodes the default image (IHDR's size; `png` refuses an `fcTL` outside it), TIFF its first IFD (whose size
   `dimensions()` is), ICO its largest entry (`dimensions()` is the inner image's header, which `image` checks
   against the entry), animated WebP its first frame into the canvas (`image-webp` refuses a frame outside the
   canvas). Tests: `memory.rs` (a 1 × 1 screen with a 16,385², a 65,535² or a second 40,000² frame: `too_large`,
   peak live heap < 4 MiB; each allocated 1 GiB or more before), `decode.rs` (an encoder-made 10 × 10 frame on a
   patched 1 × 1 screen: refused at `max_pixels` 99, decoded at 100; a P-DECODE seed). The review's files decode as:
   144 MP frame `Ok 1x1` in 160 ms; 268 MP and 1,024 MP frames `too_large` in 2 and 10 µs.
5. *F3, `quick --binary` of streamed sources.* W12a note 3 sent every pair of equal reported lengths through the
   visitor, whose streaming path fills `threads` whole 8 MiB chunks a side before `f` runs: a pair of unmapped
   sources (archive members, remote back-ends, `MmapPolicy::Never`, local files below `min_len`) that differs at
   byte 0 read 8 MiB a side at `threads` 1 and 32 MiB at 4 (what `hikasa-session` passes), and held 2 × threads ×
   8 MiB of buffers per pair, where M1 read and held 1 MiB a side. `compare_sources` and `crc32_source` now visit
   only *in place* (`chunks::visit_in_place`: mapped under the policy, or every source held in memory, which needs
   no buffer); any other source, and a discarded mapped visit, takes M1's streaming path (`compare_stream`,
   `crc32_stream`: one `buffer_size` buffer a side on the calling thread, stopping at the first difference). The
   visitor stays the one owner of the chunked passes (D-325): the mapped and in-memory comparison, the CRC, and
   hex's None scan, chunking and find; results are unchanged (the hikasa-vfs suites, A12.1). `StreamOptions::threads`
   documents the split. `tests/compare_memory.rs` (counting allocator; a generated 64 MiB streamed source): a
   difference at 0, at 5 MiB + 3 and at the last byte reads at most 1 MiB, 6 MiB and 64 MiB a side, the pair's
   peak live heap ≤ 2 MiB + 64 KiB, a CRC's ≤ 1 MiB + 64 KiB, with 1, 4 and 16 threads (before: 8 MiB read, 8 MiB
   held at `threads` 1). G3 re-measured as W12a did (the vfs benches of the pre-W12 commit `f45246f` and of this one,
   interleaved, two rounds, release, desktop with 16 threads, load 4–14 from other agents, warm cache, a btrfs
   disk): `binary_compare_2gb` `identical/auto` 1.41 and 1.65 × `sequential_read` before, 1.62 and 1.63 × after;
   `identical/stream` (M1's path both times) 0.97 and 1.05 ×, 0.95 and 0.98 ×; `crc32_1gb` `crc32/auto` 1.55 and
   1.68 ×, 1.62 and 1.58 ×: G3 (≥ 0.9 ×) met, unchanged within the noise. G10's None scan row (`gates.rs`, release,
   load 17): the 4 GiB scan 4.74 s = 0.61 × `compare_sources` of two identical 4 GiB files (7.83 s; ≤ 1.25 ×), peak
   0.35 MiB: met. (The same run's find took 0.28 s, so its cancel row, which cancels after 300 ms, found the search
   finished: a warm cache on an idle disk makes that row's input too small for the machine; not a finding of this
   fix.)
6. *Mutation survivors.* Each of the review's surviving mutations has a test or is argued equivalent; every
   mutation below was re-applied to the fixed tree (debug, `MemoryMax=8G`, nextest of the crate; script
   `/var/tmp/hikasa-work/w12-fix/mut/run.py`, log `mut.log`) and reverted. Equivalent: **H9** (`bucket_start` by
   floor): the thumbnail loop recomputes the bucket of the next column with `bucket()`, so a cut one column early
   only splits a bucket's columns over two iterations of the same bucket (the per-bucket test of A12.3 passes under
   it); **P8** (Reinhard `v > 0`: 0 / (1 + 0) = 0), **P12** (`+ 32,768`: 255 · v mod 65,535 is a multiple of 255,
   never 32,767) and **H18** (windows not multiples of 8 MiB: the counts do not depend on the cuts), as the review
   found. The review's scratch window-seam test planted three hits per edge over each other (only the last one
   survived, 6 bytes before the edge), so H1 survived it; the committed test plants one hit per edge.

**W12c.** Interpretations and extensions of §1.12.21–§1.12.29 and §1.12.32 (commits `51c2119`…, on `feat/m2`):

1. *Warnings, jobs.* `WarningCode` gains `input_changed`, `sections_truncated`, `color_profile_ignored`,
   `aspect_ratio_differs`, `frames_ignored`, `orientation_applied`; `JobKind` gains `hex_compare` (also `hex dump`),
   `hex_find`, `picture_compare`. `hex_warning` and `picture_warning` map the engines' codes one to one.
2. *`PictureComparator`* lives in `hikasa-picture` (`comparator.rs`): both files read whole (512 MiB each; above it a
   1 MiB streamed byte comparison with `rules_size_limit`), identical bytes are `binary_same` before decoding, an
   `unsupported` side gives the byte result with `fell_back_to_binary`, any other decode error is the pair's `error`.
   `Service::picture_comparator` fills its tolerance, Auto Scale, tone map and pixel limit from the Picture Compare
   defaults session; `RulesDispatch::with_pictures` adds the arm after Table and before text; `quick --rules` takes
   the same comparator for a Picture-kind pair. The *Picture Files* preset is the Picture format (its mask holds
   `*.dds`, which falls back to bytes).
3. *Errors.* `ApiError::Hex(HexError)` and `ApiError::Picture(PictureError, Option<spec>)` (the message names the
   spec when the engine's does not); a read failure of either side is `LoadFailed` with its side. `ReportError::Input
   { kind, message }` carries a read error of a hex document met while a report is written.
4. *Words.* Every word is parsed in `api/hex.rs`/`api/picture.rs` with the engines' parsers; sizes (`--block`,
   `--skew`, `--window`, `--preview`, `--length`) take the size words of `parse_byte_size` (`8k`, `1MiB`, bytes) and are
   checked by the engine's range parser; `--budget` and `--unlocked-max` are MiB numbers. `hex compare --display`
   takes `all`, `differences` (default), `same` and `none`.
5. *Human output of `hex compare`.* With `differences`: one line per listed section, `0x<addr> L <n>  R <m>  <kind>
   <preview> | <preview>`, where the address is the left offset (the right one for a right-only section) and
   `<left>/<right>` when both sides hold bytes at different offsets (Fast and Complete shift them), `—` for an empty side,
   ` …` after a cut preview, then `... N more sections (--max-sections 0 lists all)`; with `all` or `same`: the rows of
   the side-by-side report's body under that filter; with `none`: no line. Then the summary line and `verdict:
   <content kind>` (no command printed a verdict line before: `quick` has none); `picture compare` ends the same way.
6. *`hex dump`* prints `ADDRESS  hex  chars` rows (the layout's groups; decimal addresses right-aligned) and with
   `--values` the panel of `values::format` under `values at <address text>:`. An `--offset` past the end shows the
   last byte; the clamp's text of `AddressQuery::resolve` is not a warning (no code fits; noted for W13's Go To).
   `--group`/`--address` with `--json` are refused (they shape the human output only).
7. *`hex find`* walks with `hikasa_text::find::files::FileWalk` over a `WalkScope` (the roots, masks, `recursive`,
   `include_hidden`, `archives` of `FilesQuery`): `text find`'s walk, moved behind a public iterator without changing
   it (its goldens are byte-identical). Each file is opened as a hex document (`unlocked_max` 16 MiB) and searched with
   `HexFinder::all` up to `min(per file, remaining)` hits; a file that cannot be read is `skipped` with `reason`
   `error` and its error report, a link to a folder `filtered`. The CLI collects the lines of the events and prints them
   at the end (at most `--max-matches` lines).
8. *JSON.* `sections_truncated` is the engine's cut (`max_sections` of the alignment), `sections_shown` the sections the
   document lists (`--max-sections`, default 20); `warnings` of the four documents are the envelope's `Warning`
   objects. `picture compare`'s `options.blend` is 50 outside blend mode. The four JSON Schemas describe the `result`
   (neither kind has a JSON report layout, so no `schema` key) and are validated by `hikasa-report`'s
   `golden_hex_picture.rs`, whose test validator learnt `pattern`, `maximum`, `minItems`, `maxItems`.
9. *Reports.* `ReportKind::Hex` takes `display-all|-differences|-same|-none`, `context-<n>` (0…64), `line-numbers` /
   `no-line-numbers` (addresses) and refuses the words of other kinds; `ReportKind::Picture` takes `ignore-unimportant`,
   `full-size`, `mode-tolerance|-range|-blend` (`mode-blend` keeps the comparison's percentage when it blends, else 50)
   and `checkerboard`. The hex report's `--display` default is `all`, as the table's (the command's own default,
   `differences`, is its human output's); `hex compare --context <n>` becomes the word `context-<n>`. A picture report
   without `--report`'s layout is the summary (`report_request(Picture, "summary")`, scripts included); the side-by-side
   layout has no text form, and `picture compare --report side-by-side` without `--html` is refused before anything
   is read. Scaled images use the renderer's level `k` (box filter of `2ᵏ × 2ᵏ`) whose long side first fits 1,024
   pixels, so a 2,100-pixel picture is embedded 525 pixels wide. Base64 is in-house (no crate).
10. *`--diff-output`.* `Service::picture_write` renders at full resolution with the theme's colours and encodes with
    `PngLevel::Fast`; a file (or archive member) is written through `write_output_with`; `-` comes back as
    `PictureWritten::stdout` and `clipboard://` as `ClipboardImage`, which the CLI writes or places with
    `ClipboardProvider::write_image`. `-` with `--json` and `-` with a report on stdout are refused; with `-` the human
    output is left out (stdout carries the PNG). `printer` and `browser` are refused.
11. *Colours.* `Service::picture_colors` reads the selected scheme's `[picture]` from `theme.toml` with `follow_os` as
    light; reports, `--diff-output` and the clipboard use them.
12. *Sessions.* `[rules.hex]` holds `alignment` and the sizes as numbers (`HexRulesFile`), `[rules.picture]` its words
    and numbers (`PictureRulesFile`); `[view]` and `[display]` stay tables read as words when a session runs
    (`hex_layout_words_of`, `picture_geometry_words_of`), checked by `session edit --set` through the same parsers.
    Unknown keys are kept by the D-70 writer (a pre-W12 opaque `[rules]` loads and saves back its keys).
    `SessionRules::Opaque` stays for embedders, unused by any type. `session run` gains `--max-sections`, `--preview`,
    `--diff-output`, `--diff-pane`, `--checkerboard` and `--probe` (each refused for the other types); a hex session's
    `[view]` layout keys are no flags, so its `--json` run is not refused.
13. *IPC.* `OpenOptions::{hex, picture}` carry `HexWords` and `PictureWords`; `open_view_request` turns both kinds into
    `ViewRequest::Hex { request, layout, filter }` and `::Picture { request, geometry, mode }`, and `check_open` leaves
    them to the GUI (not served), so `hex compare --gui` and `picture compare --gui` call `check_hex_words` /
    `check_picture_words` first. The GUI's matches gained the two arms: a request that ever reached a model builder would
    show the two files in Text Compare (the server answers `unsupported_view` before).
14. *Scripts.* `hex-report` and `picture-report` take a session of their type or two files and `output-to:` (as
    `table-report`); `ReportFor::Hex` and `ReportFor::Picture` give the checker their slots; `media-report`,
    `version-report` and `registry-report` stay refused.
15. *Architecture (A12.27).* Check 3: `hikasa-report` and `hikasa-session` gain both crates. Checks 2 and 7 gain
    `w12_violations`: `std::fs`, `std::process`, `std::net`, `SystemTime`, `Instant::now`, `memmap2` nowhere in the two
    engines' `src/`; `image::`, `use image`, `image as` only under `core/hikasa-picture/src/codec/` and its tests;

**W12c review fixes.** Findings of the adversarial review of W12c (F1–F11), its open items and its 34 surviving
mutations (commits `bf03064`…, on `feat/m2`):

1. *F1, a Picture format's conversion in the content test.* New trait `hikasa_picture::PictureConverter { fn
   convert(&self, name, input: &[u8], ctl) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, PictureError> }` and the field
   `PictureComparator::converter`. The Service's implementation (`PictureConversions`, made by
   `picture_comparator_with(overrides, forced)`) detects each name's Picture format with the dispatcher's FF-002
   overrides, or takes the format `quick --format` forces for both sides, and runs `convert_picture`, the function
   `picture_load` runs for a side with a conversion (T11). Identical inputs are `binary_same` before any program runs;
   a converted side decodes from the output without a name hint and never from its own bytes; a failed program is the
   pair's `error` (`invalid_data`, as `picture compare` exits 100); an output the decoders do not support falls back to
   the inputs' bytes (they differ: `binary_different`). A conversion's input is bounded at 2 GiB (`too_large` above;
   it was read without the check).
2. *F2, the hex conversion's output.* `write_converted` makes a folder `hikasa-hex-*` in the temp folder with
   `tempfile::Builder` (fresh name, 0700 on Unix) and the file `converted-*.out` in it (`O_EXCL`, 0600); the document
   keeps both (`ConvertedOutput`: the file's `TempPath`, then the `TempDir`) and they are removed when it is dropped.
   `tempfile` moves from `hikasa-session`'s dev-dependencies to its dependencies (§0.4; check 3's row). A grep of W12's
   diff finds no other write into the temp folder outside tests (`--diff-output` and reports go through
   `write_output_with`; `run_external` has its private folders).
3. *F3, memory of a picture comparison.* (a) `decode_vec(Vec<u8>, …)` drops the file as soon as `image` has filled its
   buffer, before the normalization; `decode`, `decode_pair`, the Service and the comparator use it (`decode_bytes(&[u8])`
   stays for callers that keep their bytes). (b) The normalization consumes the buffer: the types of at most 4 bytes a
   pixel are written by a `TrustedLen` iterator straight into the shared `Arc<[u8]>` (no intermediate `Vec`, no copy;
   before: the native buffer, a `Vec` and its copy into the `Arc`); RGB16, RGBA16 and the float types are converted
   from their end in steps of 2¹⁸ pixels into a zeroed buffer (fresh pages, resident only once written) while the
   source is truncated and shrunk behind each step, then moved into the `Arc`. (c) `decode_two` estimates each side's
   peak from its header (`decode_peak` = file + the decoder's buffer + 4 bytes a pixel) and decodes both in parallel when
   the two fit `PARALLEL_DECODE_BUDGET` (256 MiB), else one after the other in the order that holds less (the first
   side's picture stays while the second decodes). The Service reads the left side (and runs its conversion) first:
   when that side alone estimates more than half the budget it is decoded before the right file is read (a large pair
   never holds both files beside a decoder's buffer), else the right side is read and `decode_two` decodes both; the
   comparator reads both (it compares their bytes first), then `decode_two`. (d) A `--diff-output` file is compressed
   straight into the target (`encode_png_to`, a `Write`): the PNG is never held whole (stdout and the clipboard keep
   their buffers). A reader-streamed decode was not taken: the VFS's readers seek, but
   `image`'s JPEG decoder reads its input whole and the content test holds both files to compare their bytes first.
   `memory.rs` (counting allocator) bounds the peak live heap of a noisy 1,024² PNG's decode by max(file + pixels,
   pixels + result) + 1.5 MiB for RGB8 (measured 6.3 MiB; without the early drop of the file 10.0 MiB) and by
   max(file + pixels, 2 × result) + 1.5 MiB for RGBA16 (measured 16.3 MiB; without it 20.0 MiB), and two RGB8 pictures
   decoded one after the other by result + pixels + result + 0.75 MiB = 11.75 MiB (decoded in parallel they measured
   12.7 MiB). G11's end-to-end row uses photo-like inputs (§1.12.28, figures below).
4. *F4, `--dry-run` with `--diff-output`.* `PictureCompareRequest::dry_run` (the CLI sets it from `--dry-run`): nothing
   is rendered or written; `PictureCompareResponse::planned` = `PlannedImage { line, file }` (`write <spec>`, `replace
   <spec>`, `write the image to standard output`, `copy the image to the clipboard`); the JSON's `diff_output` has the
   area's size. `ReportOutcome::also` (set by the adapter) lists the image before `would write <n> files`, a file
   counted. `--diff-output -` with `--dry-run` is not refused with a report on stdout (only the plan is written).
5. *F5.* *Picture Files*: `*.png;*.apng;*.jpg;*.jpeg;*.jpe;*.jfif;*.gif;*.bmp;*.ico;*.tif;*.tiff;*.webp;*.tga;*.pnm;
   *.ppm;*.pgm;*.pbm;*.pam;*.qoi;*.exr;*.hdr;*.dds` (every extension of a supported container in `image` 0.25.10's
   `ImageFormat::from_extension`, and `.jpe`), description *Images (compared by their pixels; DDS by bytes).* (docs/10,
   `help/format.md`, the `format list` goldens).
6. *F6.* The comparator keeps the warnings of both pictures and of the comparison that are not informational
   (`color_profile_ignored`, `aspect_ratio_differs`) in `ContentOutcome::warnings`; `PictureWarning::to_warning` maps
   the codes (the Service's `picture_warning` calls it).
7. *F7.* `diff_output_target(raw)`: `-` → stdout, `clipboard://` (any case) → the clipboard, every other word a file;
   the printer and browser refusal of `picture_compare` is gone (`picture_write` keeps it for its other callers).
8. *F8.* `Service::refuse_output_onto_inputs(flag, raw, [left, right])`: the target is refused (`invalid_input`, *<flag>
   <spec>: it is the left input; an output never replaces an input*) when its resolved spec equals an input's (an
   archive member included) or when both exist and have the same file id (a link, a hard link). Standard input and
   the clipboard are no files. `picture_compare` checks `--diff-output`; the CLI's picture and hex report paths check
   a file target of `--output`/`--output-to` before the comparison. Text and folder reports keep M1's behaviour.
9. *F9.* `hex dump --offset`: `+n` counts from 0, `end` is the last byte, an offset at or past the end of a non-empty
   file is refused (*--offset 1000: past the end of … (1000 bytes; the last byte is at 0x3E7)*), a negative one before
   reading; an empty file dumps nothing at offset 0. `AddressQuery::resolve`'s clamp stays for W13's Go To.
10. *F10.* D-374: `Service::picture_rules_on_defaults`, `hex_rules_on_defaults`; the CLI's `request_of` of both
    subcommands (so `--gui` sends the same words) and the scripts' two-file forms call them.
11. *F11.* (a) `session run` of a hex session refuses `--ignore-unimportant` (`not_for_hex`). (b) `hex compare` refuses the
    layout flags and `--context` when neither `--json` nor a report is asked and the display prints sections
    (`differences`, the default) or nothing (`none`): `hex_display_shows_rows`; `session run` of a hex session refuses
    `--context` likewise (a session's `[view]` keys stay silent). (c) `PictureCompareRequest::view_checkerboard`: a
    session's `[view] checkerboard` (default on) is the image's when `--checkerboard` is not given. (d) `hex dump`'s
    read errors are the VFS's, without a side. (e) A size word refused by its range names the word typed (`"3k"`).
    (f) New `PictureError::AreaTooLarge { width, height, pixels, limit }` (`too_large`; *the compared area is W × H =
    P pixels, more than the L pixels an image may have*) for the render limit and an area beyond 2³² − 1. (g) `session
    run --help` names the six types; `picture compare` has its own report flags (`PictureReportArgs`: no byte
    addresses, layouts summary and side-by-side).
12. *Open item 2.* §1.12.23's `--display` list gains `same` and `none` (W12c note 4 already took them).
13. *Open item 7, handles on Windows.* `LocalVfs` keeps the standard library's `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`: refusing it would
    block other programs' saves of a file a hex view holds, and the stamps (`check_unchanged`, `input_changed`,
    `stale`) already report a replacement. §1.12.3 and §6.12's table now expect the replace to succeed on Windows too
    (W12a note 23's question answered).
14. *Open item 5.* A `ViewRequest::Hex` or `::Picture` that reached the GUI's model builder opened the two files in
    Text Compare; it now opens Home with the error *view kind `hex_compare` is not supported in this version* (the
    server still answers `unsupported_view` first; W13 replaces the arm).
15. *Open item 4.* D-331's conversion rows 1, 2 and 13 and F1's picture rows run through the binary with `/bin/sh`
    programs (`cli_hex_picture_fixes.rs`, Unix only; `exec` keeps dash out of the way).
16. *A flaky test.* `cli_interrupt` `a8_14_a_second_ctrl_c_ends_a_script_at_once` sent the first Ctrl-C as soon as the
    handler was set; on a loaded machine it could come before the script blocked on standard input, be seen, and end
    the run, so the second press found no process. The test now tries again (up to eight times, each later) when the
    run ends on the first press or was already ending when the second came, and asserts the second press's exit
    otherwise.

G11 end to end re-measured (release, desktop with 16 threads and 61 GiB, load 5–7 from other agents, warm cache;
`perf_gates.rs` `g11_picture_compare_end_to_end`, photo-like 6000 × 4000 RGB8 PNGs of 72.1 MB written in stored
blocks, `--diff-output`): **0.36 s, peak RSS 326.2 MiB** (≤ 3.5 × 96 MB + 64 MiB = 384.4 MiB): **met** (the review's
photo-like pair took 516.5 MiB; the stages: 361.3 MiB with (a)–(c), 325.2 MiB with (d), 326.2 MiB with the left side
decoded first). **Known row, RGBA16:** the same pair as 16-bit RGBA takes 0.44 s and **472.4 MiB** with its stored
192 MB files, 386.0 MiB with 105 MB files (ImageMagick, fast compression) and 452.0 MiB with 177 MB files (full 16-bit
noise): the second decode holds the first picture (96 MB), its own file and its 192 MB native buffer, so the row is met
only below a file of about 100 MB; streaming the decoder from the VFS reader (no file held) would meet it and is left
open (the GUI's budget, D-372, is measured on 12 MP pictures). `hikasa-picture`'s G11 rows after the change: decode of
a 24 MP PNG 130.6 ms, diff 10.9 ms, renders 15.0–34.0 ms, geometry median 6.5 ms, worst 7.3 ms, cancel 0.7 and 3.4 ms:
all met.

### 1.13 W13 — GUI Hex and Picture views, report dialog, Quick Compare dialog

**Ids.** HX-001 (the hex panes: address column with its toggle, hex bytes in groups, the ASCII/Latin-1 column, the
Layout dialog, multi-GB files open at once), HX-002 (the alignment chosen in the window: the *Alignment* switch and the
Alignment tab), HX-003 (the pane's Hex format picker, *Converted*), HX-004 (byte colours, gaps, the thumbnail, File Info,
display font commands), HX-005 (display filters with context rows, Next/Previous Difference Bytes, Next/Previous Existing
Byte, Go To, Find, Find Next/Previous, Next/Previous Difference Files in a child view), HX-007 (Current Byte Address,
the value panel), PX-002 (three panes side by side or stacked, File Info headers, zoom, synchronized panning, full
screen), PX-003 (the mode switch, the Tolerance spinner, the Blend slider, Blend Toggle, Ignore Unimportant), PX-004
(Auto Scale, rotations, flips, the offset drag and nudges, Reset Difference Offset), PX-007 (the checkerboard option, the
background), PX-008 (status bar, Picture Compare Info), PX-009 (Edit ▸ Copy of the picked pane, Open Clipboard), UI-023
(the `[picture]` colours in the window, live), RPT-001 (*<Type> Report…* in every view whose type has a report kind:
Text Compare, Folder Compare, Folder Sync, Table Compare, Hex Compare, Picture Compare), RPT-003 (one report dialog),
RPT-002's printer as Q6 answered (*Print Preview*, *View in Browser*), CLI-005 (the Quick Compare dialog at startup,
OPT-001's three keys), SES-001 and SES-020 (hex and picture sessions saved, restored, in workspaces; their rule tabs),
FC-062 (Open With ▸ *Hex Compare*, *Picture Compare*; Open chooses those views by file format; *Compare Files Using*),
CLI-G03 and CLI-003 (`hex compare --gui`, `picture compare --gui`, `gui open` of picture and hex pairs, `--fv` served),
UI-005 (hex and picture context menus), UI-008 (drops onto their panes), UI-030 (their status items), the GUI rows of
gates G10 and G11, ARCH-GUI-003 re-measured. Decisions D-353…D-373.

**Out of scope.** HX-006 editing, Replace, Save, *Copy to Right/Left* of bytes (P1; the panes' caret model is ready
for it, §1.13.24); PX-005 Replacements and PX-006 metadata with `CompareTags` (P1); FC-079 *File Compare Report…* over a
folder selection (P1); Find in Files of byte patterns in the window (`hikasa hex find` is the headless form; P1);
Media, Version and Registry views (M3 and later); native printing (D-62); the Table views (complete,
`m2-table-contract.md` phase 3 — only its report dialog is replaced by W13's, D-366); the real-GPU and laptop figures
(W14, the maintainer).

This section is written like §1.9 and §1.11: the **GUI's needs** — toolkit-free models tested without a window, the
drawing split, the `Service` calls (§1.13.20, *exists* or *new*), the catalogue ids, keys, persistence, errors and
cancellation. Every rule that decides a byte state, an aligned segment, a section, an address text, a value, a find hit,
a pixel class, a rendered pixel, a statistic, a report's bytes, a quick verdict or a view kind stays core's (W7, W12;
T11, D-105); W13 adds geometry, textures, input, focus and the order of dialogs. The core additions (§1.13.20) are typed
forms of what the engines already do, or pure helpers the CLI could share; each part lands its share in its first
commits, separate from the GUI.
