### 6.3 W3 acceptance

- A3.1 **Primitives (D-92, D-99).** One table test per primitive, run on `MemoryVfs` (case-sensitive and
  case-insensitive) and on `LocalVfs` in a tempdir (host path syntax; Windows and macOS rows run on those
  platforms, the maintainer's platform run before merge): rows for a missing item, a file, an empty folder, a
  non-empty folder, a link to a file, a link to a folder, a broken link, an existing target with and without
  `replace`, a case-only rename, a missing parent with and without `parents`, a non-folder ancestor; each row
  states the outcome or the error kind. `set_times` with and without `created` (`SET_CREATED` per platform);
  `set_attrs` `Mode` (Unix), `Dos` `R` and an unsupported bit (Windows), the wrong family. The capability table
  of §1.3.1 per back-end; the router dispatch table (local, blobs, an unsupported scheme, mixed kinds).
- A3.2 **Errors (D-93).** Every new `VfsError` variant: kind, message, `spec()`, the `io::Error` round trip;
  `from_io` of `DirectoryNotEmpty` and `CrossesDevices`; `ErrorKind::NotEmpty` serde `"not_empty"`; the §2.21
  table test still total (`vfs` → 100); `VfsOp::ALL` and `Capabilities::names` (21, canonical bit order).
- A3.3 **Copy (ARCH-031, D-95).** Table tests on `MemoryVfs` → `MemoryVfs` (two instances: another back-end),
  `MemoryVfs` → itself and `LocalVfs` → `LocalVfs`: file, empty file, folder tree, preserve on/off, created time;
  the journal shows content (`commit`) → `set_times` → `set_attrs` per file and each folder's metadata after its
  last child; a target without `SET_TIMES`/`SET_ATTRS` gives exactly one `capability_missing` warning and done
  items; a failing `set_attrs` fails the item and keeps the content; owner never changes. The local fast path and
  the streamed path give the same bytes, times and mode (a file of 64 MiB + 1 byte takes the streamed path).
- A3.4 **Faults (D-95, D-103).** Property test over generated trees (≤ 50 items) × fault position × fault op
  (`Open`, `Read`, `Write`, `Commit`, `Mkdir`, `SetTimes`, `SetAttrs`, `Symlink`, `Remove`, `Rename`, read and write
  errors after N bytes): the failing item's target is exactly as before (`dump()` equal for that path; no

### 6.5 W5 acceptance

Rules for every item: fixtures are **generated in the tests** by `core/hikasa-vfs/tests/common/archives.rs` (a tree as data → bytes
of each format; hostile members as raw bytes: tar headers built by hand with their checksum, because `tar::Builder` refuses
them, zip records patched after writing), never downloaded and never committed as binaries. **Every test runs on Linux,
Windows and macOS** (CI runs all three): no real links, FIFOs or devices on disk (link and device members are bytes in an
archive); no hard-coded `/tmp` or `/`-only paths (specs from `Spec::parse` on a `tempfile` folder, canonicalized because
macOS' temp folder is a link); Windows path rows use `resolve_with` and `PathStyle::Windows`, so they run everywhere; time zones
by `TimeZone::fixed` and POSIX strings, no time-zone database; readers dropped before a folder is removed (Windows); Unix-only
checks (`0700`) behind `cfg(unix)`; goldens normalize the temp prefix and separators as the existing CLI tests do. No test
reads the real clock, zone or home folder (T1). The part of each item is in brackets.

- A5.1 **Spec model (D-137) [W5a].** Table test of `Spec::parent`, `file_name`, `container`, `outermost_file`, `archive_depth`
  and `canonical` for a root, a member, a nested member and a nested root, Unix and Windows styles; `ops::check_item` refuses
  a root. Property P-ARCH-1: generated nested specs over a generated tree round-trip through `canonical`, `Spec::parse` and
  `resolve_spec`, and `Serialize` refuses a lossy base as before. `Spec::parse` never yields `ArchiveMember` (the M1 table
  of 30 rows is unchanged).
- A5.2 **Resolution (D-138) [W5a].** Every row of §1.5.4 through `resolve_with` and a table-driven fake, in both path styles
  where the row applies, on every platform; rows 1–23, 27 and 28 again through `resolve_spec` on `ArchiveVfs` over
  `MemoryVfs` and over `LocalVfs` in a tempdir (host syntax). Call counts: at most one `stat` per component; rows 4, 6 and
  28 never open the archive (`open` journal empty). Determinism: the same 1,000 specs resolved from 8 threads, in any
  order, give the same answers. A source check: `resolve.rs` names neither `std::fs` nor `std::env`.
- A5.3 **Formats (D-136) [W5a].** One generated tree in each of the ten formats (one member for the four streams), plus a
  tree with 300-byte names: `list`, `stat`, `open_read` equal the tree, on `MemoryVfs` and `LocalVfs` containers. Nested `a.zip/b.tar.gz/c.txt`
  and three levels. Concatenated gz, bz2, xz, zst. Member names of single streams (`x.txt.gz`, `noext.gz`-style cases). Masks: `.JAR`
  as zip, a disabled `tar_gz` makes `x.tar.gz` a one-member `gz`, a custom mask, an empty mask. The capability table per format
  and per nesting; the router table, with and without `with_archives`; `child` of root and folder; synthesized folders; the root's
  entry; every `Entry` column of §1.5.5. `FollowLinks::Yes` leaves a link member a link without an `EntryError`.
- A5.4 **Content reads (D-139) [W5a].** Zip members of 1 MiB and 1 MiB + 1 byte take memory and the cache (a counter). A plain tar
  member reads with no cache file and `Seek` in any order. Compressed tar: the first read decodes only up to its member and
  spools it, the second distinct read writes the whole stream once, later reads decode nothing (test counters), and a stream
  bigger than the free cache keeps spooling member by member. Every reader passes the same seek and read table. 8 threads on
  one archive give the same bytes. `tar_walk`: PAX `size` over the header, GNU long names and links, base-256 sizes, `g`
  headers, labels, an old V7 header; an extension body of 1 MiB + 1 byte is damage.
- A5.5 **Cache (D-140) [W5a].** The location for each `ConfigMode` and platform by a pure table (`resolve_config_dir`). A command
  that only lists creates no folder. Layout: numeric names, `0700` on Unix. Accounting: `used` equals the files' lengths in a
  random workload; `cache_max` evicts least recently used files, never one a reader holds; a member over the limit is
  `ArchiveLimit` and leaves nothing. Reuse: a second read decodes nothing. Invalidation: touching the container (new stamp) drops the
  index and the files. Exit: `cleanup` and `Drop` remove everything. Crash: a leftover `s7/` with an unlocked `s7.lock` goes
  at the next session's first spool; a folder whose lock is held (a second handle in the test) stays. Two `ArchiveVfs`
  on one root get different numbers. Concurrent sessions on one root, threads (`concurrent_sessions_on_one_root_keep_their_bytes`,
  `a_live_session_survives_a_crowd_of_sweeps`) and processes (`concurrent_processes_read_their_own_members`), each read
  their own bytes; a replaced cache file is decoded again; a reader keeps its bytes when the path is replaced.
- A5.6 **Names (D-141) [W5a].** Rules 1–4 and 17 as tables, for zip and tar each: `../x`, `a/../../x`, `/etc/passwd`, `\x`,
  `\\srv\x`, `C:\x`, `C:/x`, `c:x`, `..\..\x`, `a\b`, NUL, 4,097 bytes, `./a//b`, `.`, `./`, invalid UTF-8, CP437, duplicates in both
  orders, `a` with `a/b` in both orders, `A.txt` with `a.txt`; rows `<refused-N>`, the cap of 1,000, the warning's total. An
  end-to-end test extracts each hostile archive with `vfs cp -r a.zip/ out/` and asserts that the tempdir holds only what lies
  below `out/` and that the cache held numeric names only. The pure Windows name check of rule 17 on every platform, `LocalVfs::child`
  on Windows.

  `OperationUnsupported`, lookups through them `NotADirectory`, a member below one refused, a copy out skips them with one

### 6.6 W6 acceptance

Rules for every item:

- **Platforms.** Every test runs on Linux, Windows and macOS unless it says otherwise; Windows and macOS are exercised
  only by CI and wine, so what differs is stated. Core logic runs on `MemoryVfs` with case sensitivity as a parameter,
  so a case rule never depends on the host: Windows and macOS temp folders are case-insensitive, and no disk test may
  assume a case. Disk tests use `tempfile`, canonicalized (macOS' temp folder is a link), with specs from `Spec::parse`;
  goldens normalize the temp prefix and separators as the existing CLI tests do.
- **Unix only (`cfg(unix)`):** modes, FIFOs, devices, sockets, `Entry::special` from disk. **Windows only
  (`cfg(windows)`):** DOS `R`, `S`, `H` set with real attributes. The rest of the attribute tables run on `MemoryVfs`
  with `Attrs::Dos`, everywhere. Real symbolic links: `cfg(unix)`, or on Windows skipped when `create_symlink` answers
  `PermissionDenied`, as A3.6; link rules are also tested on `MemoryVfs`. The four tests that fail only under wine
  (`a3_1_rename_case_only`, `a3_1_set_times_created_local`, `a3_6_rule4`, `a3_6_rule9`) are not a W6 regression; no new
  test may depend on wine's rename or file times: such a check goes behind `cfg(not(windows))` with a note, and runs on
  real Windows in CI.
- **Times.** A test sets times with `set_times` to whole seconds; never relies on a file system's granularity, nor on
  "now". Real clock, zone and home folder are never read (T1). `created` is `cfg(any(windows, target_os = "macos"))` or
  `MemoryVfs`.
- **No timers.** Tests do not sleep or race a clock. Cancellation is deterministic: a `ProgressSink` or fault hook
  cancels the token at the n-th item or byte, and the test asserts results, not time. W6 needs no wall-clock assertion.
  One that a part must add goes through `tests/common/timing.rs::meets_in_some_round(bound, measure)`, with `cancel` in
  the test's name (D-69): one round and the bound on Linux; on macOS and Windows up to six rounds, the fastest meeting
  the bound and the worst meeting G4, the rule of `core/hikasa-folder/tests/budget.rs`, because shared runners deliver
  wake-ups late for seconds at a time. Waiting on a job polls a state, bounded by count, never by a fixed sleep.
- **Faults.** `MemoryVfs` hooks of §1.3.8; `dump()` proves "untouched". New test-only hooks are allowed on `MemoryVfs`.
  Recycle bin on `MemoryVfs::trashed()`, as CI has no usable bin; a real bin stays in `tests/trash.rs`'s existing cases.
  Programs, clipboard, terminal: `RecordingLauncher`, `FixedClipboard`, and a scripted line source; no real program, no
  PTY.
- **GUI.** Headless through the models (§1.4.16); window tests only under `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY xvfb-run -a`.
- **Gates** run on Linux only, `#[ignore]`, by hand. Everything else is on CI. The part of each item is in brackets.

**W6a — Foundations**

- A6.1 **Batch plans (D-162) [W6a].** `core/hikasa-vfs/tests/ops_batch.rs`. A hand-built `OpKind::Batch` mixing
  `create_dir`, `copy`, `link`, `move`, `remove`, `remove_dir`, `touch` runs on `MemoryVfs`: journal order equals plan
  order; `times` per item; `Preserve` of `BatchOptions`; a failed folder cuts its subtree and no sibling root
  (`not_run`); declined `skip` blocks a parent's `remove_dir` (`children_failed`). `moves` gives two-phase behaviour
  into an archive. `execute` still equals `execute_with` with default options on every existing W3 and W5 test.
  `PlanItem` round-trips through JSON with and without the new fields, a W3 plan text reads. `hikasa.vfs_op.v1` goldens
  unchanged. A panic inside `execute_with` aborts batches as A5.14.
- A6.2 **Stamps (D-163) [W6a].** `ops_batch.rs`. Every field × source and target: changed size, time, kind, a gone item,

### 6.7 W7 acceptance

Rules for every item: those of §6.6 (platforms, times, no timers, faults, GUI, gates), and:

- **Tests can fail.** Each property test of W7 (P-OPS's extension in A7.1, P-RPTREQ, P-IL, P-XML, P-FXML, P-LINKS,
  P-WRITE, the streaming test) is checked by mutation: at least one hand mutation of the code it guards (a named change
  in a named file: a dropped condition, a swapped side, an off-by-one, a skipped escape, a missing stamp check) makes it
  fail, and is reverted. §1.7.20 lists, per part, each mutation, the test that caught it and the seed where there is
  one; a property no mutation fails is rewritten until one does. `cargo mutants` may be run on `hikasa-report`, but its
  report does not replace the list. A check against a tool (`xmllint`, A7.7) has a negative case, so a skipped or
  stubbed check cannot pass silently where it is required.
- **Platform blind spots.** Names that are not valid UTF-8 come from Linux trees: on disk on Linux (`cfg(target_os =
  "linux")`), on `MemoryVfs` everywhere, and on macOS the disk part asserts that APFS refuses the name and stops there,
  as commit `f85fba3` did. Windows spellings of a target (`C:\…`, `\\?\C:\…`, forward slashes, spaces, `#`, `%`) run on
  disk under `cfg(windows)` and as a pure-function table everywhere. Case-insensitive file systems: Windows and macOS CI
  temp folders are, Linux's is not, and `MemoryVfs` with folding gives the same case on every host. Line endings: every
  report is `\n` on every platform (CSV `\r\n`), goldens compare bytes (`.gitattributes` `* -text`), CRLF, CR and mixed
  inputs are fixtures. Windows tests also run under wine on Linux before each push, and the heavy proptest run once
  per part, as the maintainer's pre-push rule asks; the four wine-only failures of §6.6 stay exempt and no new test may
  join them.
- **Goldens.** Every new layout × palette has goldens: text interleaved × {text, ANSI, HTML colour, HTML mono} with and
  without each strike-out, text and folder XML, folder side-by-side HTML with links × {colour, mono}, HTML wrap × layout,
  the print block × {portrait, landscape} × {colour, mono}. `HIKASA_BLESS=1` rewrites them; a review reads every
  changed golden.
- **Help and text.** Every user-visible message W7 adds (errors, warnings, dry-run lines, help) is fixed English, appears
  in a golden or a test assertion, and every warning code is in `help/json-output.md`.

### 6.8 W8 acceptance

Rules for every item: those of §6.6 (platforms, times, no timers, faults, GUI, gates) and §6.7 (tests can fail, platform
blind spots, goldens, help and text), and:

- **Tests can fail.** Each property test of W8 (P-LEX, P-PARSE, P-EXPAND, P-SCRIPT, the stream test) and each integration
  test that stands in for one (A8.7, A8.11, A8.14) is checked by mutation (docs/17 §3 point 6): at least one named hand
  mutation of the code it guards (a dropped `""` rule, a column off by one, `lt` rewritten inside a path, an expansion
  re-lexed, a skipped refresh after a copy, a swapped direction, 107 not ending the run, a silent question answered yes)
  makes it fail, and is reverted. §1.8.20 lists each mutation, the test that caught it and the seed where there is one.
- **Scripts in tests** are files named `*.txt` under `tests/fixtures/` (Hikasa owns no script extension), written with
  `\n` unless the test is about line ends; `.gitattributes` keeps them byte for byte. Absolute paths of docs/12's
  examples are replaced by temp folders through script arguments or a generated copy, and the test says which.
- **Time.** Service tests inject the clock and the zone (`FixedClock`, a fixed `TimeZone`); CLI tests check `%date%`,
  `%time%`, `%fn_time%` by format and against the local date read before and after the run (equal unless the run spans
  midnight, then the test retries once). No test sleeps.
- **Terminals.** Questions and the stop-on-error prompt are tested through `confirm.rs`'s scripted line source; "no
  terminal" is the CI default; no PTY.

### 6.9 W9 acceptance

Rules for every item: those of §6.4 (window tests and measurements only under `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY xvfb-run -a`;
everything else headless through the models), §6.6 (platforms, times, no timers, faults, gates), §6.7 and §6.8 (tests
can fail, goldens, help and text), and:

- **Through the models.** GUI tests build `AppCore` over a temporary configuration (fixed clock and zone,
  `FixedClipboard`, `RecordingLauncher`, a private IPC endpoint) and comparisons of trees generated by the test (disk
  for the GUI tests, `MemoryVfs` where the core side is tested); they drive `execute(window, Invocation)`, the models'
  pointer and key calls, dialog models and `poll()`; jobs are awaited by polling (bounded), held by W6d's gates where a
  test needs a job in flight. No sleep, no timer; debounces take explicit frame times.
- **Drawing** is tested as shapes (§1.4.16 rule 5): headless `egui::Context::run_ui` frames give the glyphs, the
  header, the columns and the preview rows, checked by bounds and colours, never by screenshot.
- **Tests can fail.** Each property test of W9 and each integration test that stands in for one (A9.2, A9.4, A9.12,
  A9.15, A9.16, A9.19, A9.20) is checked by mutation (docs/17 §3 point 6): at least one named hand mutation of the code
  it guards (a preview line without its backup suffix, a swipe that keeps one side across the centre, a sort tie
  reversed, a selection that keeps a collapsed folder's children, an override written under the wrong path, a drop on
  the right pane copying to the left, a completion that ignores the back-end's case rule, the hollow and unopened
  glyphs swapped) makes it fail, and is reverted. §1.9.25 lists each mutation, the test that caught it and the seed
  where there is one.

**Where each runs**

| Test | Linux CI | Windows CI | macOS CI | wine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| core additions (A9.2, A9.5, A9.12, A9.15, A9.20 core, A9.22 core) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| GUI models (A9.1…A9.10, A9.13…A9.24) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| case-insensitive completion and drives (A9.5, A9.6) | pure table and `MemoryVfs` | disk | disk (APFS default) | `MemoryVfs` |
| reveal command lines (A9.22) | `RecordingLauncher` | `RecordingLauncher` | `RecordingLauncher` | `RecordingLauncher` |
| window tests (A9.25, optional) | `xvfb-run`, `#[ignore]` | — | — | — |
| G15, ARCH-GUI-003 (A9.27) | by hand, `#[ignore]`, llvmpipe | — | — | — |
| OS drag and drop, real clipboard, real file managers (A9.30) | maintainer's desktop | maintainer | maintainer | — |

### 6.10 W10 acceptance

Rules for every item: those of §6.6 (platforms, times, no timers, faults, gates), §6.7 and §6.8 (tests can fail,
platform blind spots, goldens, help and text), and:

- **Headless.** Every item is tested on core types and the Service (`MemoryVfs` where possible, disk where a back-end
  matters), never through a window: W10 has no view. Documents are generated by the tests (seeded xorshift, §6.1),
  fixtures of encodings come from `core/hikasa-formats/tests/fixtures/encoding/` plus generated legacy-encoding files;
  nothing large is committed.
- **Exactness by comparison.** Wherever a result must equal another path's (incremental vs full, a save vs the source
  bytes, `text convert` vs a view's conversion, `text find` vs `Finder`), the test compares the two complete results
  (the `hikasa.text_compare.v1` document, the file bytes, the JSON), not a summary.
- **Tests can fail.** Each property test of W10 (P-BLOCK, P-EDIT-1, P-EDIT-2, P-ALIGN-REN, P-ANCHOR, P-SAVE, P-CONVERT,
  P-FIND) and each integration test that stands in for one (A10.6, A10.13, A10.15, A10.23) is checked by mutation
  (docs/17 §3 point 6): at least one named hand mutation of the code it guards makes it fail, and is reverted. The
  mutations named in each item below are the minimum; §1.10.29 lists each mutation, the test that caught it and the seed
  where there is one.
- **Time.** Undo coalescing takes explicit `at_ms`; no test sleeps; debounces are the adapter's (W11).

**Where each runs**

| Test | Linux CI | Windows CI | macOS CI | wine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| edit model, recompare, anchors, find, navigation, details (A10.1…A10.11, A10.22, A10.25) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| save on `MemoryVfs` and disk, conversions, formats, Ignored (A10.13…A10.21) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `Vfs::writable` on disk (A10.6) | `access` (a 0o444 file, a read-only bind mount where the runner allows, else `#[ignore]` with the reason) | DOS `R`, a read-only volume by hand | `access` | DOS `R` |
| links followed by a save (A10.17) | disk | disk with developer mode, else skipped with the reason | disk | — |
| G8 (A10.12, A10.29) | by hand, `#[ignore]`, release | — | — | — |
| the counting-allocator memory tests (A10.1, A10.12) | yes | yes | yes | yes |

### 6.11 W11 acceptance

Rules for every item: those of §6.4 (window tests and measurements only under `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY xvfb-run -a`;
everything else headless through the models), §6.6 (platforms, times, no timers, faults, gates), §6.7 and §6.8 (tests
can fail, goldens, help and text), §6.9's *through the models* and *drawing* rules, §6.10's *exactness by comparison*,
and:

- **Through the models.** GUI tests build `AppCore` over a temporary configuration (fixed clock and zone,
  `FixedClipboard` with primary selection, `RecordingLauncher`, a private IPC endpoint) and text pairs generated by the
  test (seeded xorshift, §6.1; disk where a save or a watch matters, `MemoryVfs` where the core side is tested); they
  drive `execute(window, Invocation)`, the panes' key, text, IME and pointer calls with `FixedMetrics`, dialog models and
  `poll()`; jobs are awaited by polling (bounded) and held by gates where a test needs one in flight (a recompare, a
  save, a search). Frame times are explicit (`now` arguments): the debounce, the blink, the primary selection's settle
  and *Recomparing…* are tested without sleeping.
- **Exactness.** Wherever the window's result must equal core's (the view's comparison after an install and a fresh
  `compare`; a save from the window and `text_save_*` on the same documents; Replace All in a panel and `replace_all`; a
  rule tab's write and `session edit --set`; a manager action and `hikasa format …`; Find in Files' panel and `text find
  --json`), the test compares the complete results.
- **Tests can fail.** Each property test of W11 (P-CARET, P-TYPE, P-LIVE-VIEW, P-TABS-ID) and each integration test that
  stands in for one (A11.1, A11.6, A11.7, A11.8, A11.15, A11.23) is checked by mutation (docs/17 §3 point 6): the
  mutations named below are the minimum; §1.11.35 lists each, the test that caught it and the seed where there is one.

**Where each runs**

| Test | Linux CI | Windows CI | macOS CI | wine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| core additions (A11.2 cursor, A11.10, A11.21, A11.23 core, A11.25 core) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| GUI models (A11.1…A11.10, A11.12…A11.26) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| primary selection (A11.5) | `FixedClipboard`; arboard's X11 code by hand | n/a (`Unavailable`) | n/a | `Unavailable` |
| save on disk, watch, reloads (A11.7, A11.22) | disk | disk | disk (APFS) | disk |
| window tests (A11.27, optional) | `xvfb-run`, `#[ignore]` | — | — | — |
| G16, ARCH-GUI-003 (A11.11, A11.29) | by hand, `#[ignore]`, llvmpipe | — | — | — |
| IME with real input methods, real clipboards, fonts (A11.32) | maintainer's desktop | maintainer | maintainer | — |

### 6.12 W12 acceptance (hex and picture; met)

The Table half of W12 was accepted by `docs/design/m2-table-contract.md` §7 (AT.1…AT.31, met). Rules for every item
below: those of §6.6 (platforms, times, no timers, faults, gates), §6.7 and §6.8 (tests can fail, platform blind spots,
goldens, help and text), and:

- **Headless.** Every item is tested on core types, the Service and the binary, never through a window (W12 has no
  view). Inputs are generated by the tests: byte files by seeded xorshift with planted edits; pictures built in memory
  and encoded with `image`'s own encoders (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, ICO, TIFF, WebP lossless, TGA, PNM, QOI, OpenEXR, HDR).
  Committed binaries stay under 8 KiB each (a JPEG with an EXIF orientation, a PNG with an ICC profile, a truncated
  file); nothing large is committed; nothing reads the clock or the environment.
- **Exactness by comparison.** Wherever a result must equal another path's (the visitor vs the old streaming compare,
  a mapped vs a streamed visit, tiles vs a full render, `session run` vs the subcommand, a hex verdict vs `quick
  --binary`), the test compares the two complete results (segments, the JSON document, the pixel bytes), not a summary.
- **Threads.** Every property runs with 1, 4 and 16 threads (and, for the visitor, mapped and streamed) and asserts
  identical results (T2).
- **Tests can fail.** Each property test of W12 (P-VISIT, P-NONE, P-HEXALIGN, P-HEXROWS, P-HEXFIND, P-DECODE, P-PIXEL,
  P-GEOM, P-TILES, P-PICMIRROR) and each integration test that stands in for one (A12.20, A12.24, A12.25) is checked by
  mutation (docs/17 §3 point 6): at least one named hand mutation of the code it guards makes it fail, and is reverted.
  The mutations named below are the minimum; §1.12.33 lists each mutation, the test that caught it and the seed.

**Where each runs**

| Test | Linux CI | Windows CI | macOS CI | wine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| visitor, hex document on `MemoryVfs` and disk, alignments, rows, find, values (A12.1…A12.10) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| decoders, classes, geometry, rendering, statistics, PNG (A12.12…A12.17) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| mapped visits (A12.1) | yes | yes | yes | yes (mapped path as Windows) |
| an open handle vs the unlocked load (A12.2) | rename/delete while open | rename/delete while open (`FILE_SHARE_DELETE`; the stamps report the change, W12c review fixes note 13) | as Linux | as Windows |
| Service, CLI, reports, sessions, folder test, IPC (A12.19…A12.27) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| G10, G11 (A12.11, A12.18, A12.28) | by hand, `#[ignore]`, release | — | — | — |
| the counting-allocator memory tests (A12.2, A12.4, A12.18) | yes | yes | yes | yes |

**W12a — Hex engine**

- A12.1 **The chunk visitor and HX-009 (D-325) [W12a].** `core/hikasa-vfs/tests/chunks.rs`: P-VISIT — random pairs (equal;
  one side a prefix; one differing byte at random offsets including 0, every chunk edge ± 1 and the last byte; lengths
  around 0, 1, 8 MiB ± 1, 16 MiB + 3) give the same values mapped, streamed, from memory and with 1/4/16 threads; the
  lowest-offset `Break` wins; `compare_sources` and `crc32_source` give exactly W10's results (every existing test of
  `hikasa-vfs` green, plus a differential test against a naive byte loop); a truncation during a visit is
  `unexpected_eof` naming the source; the re-stat rule re-runs a changed mapped visit streaming (the existing hook).
  HX-009 at engine level: for those pairs `hikasa_hex` None, Fast and Complete give the verdict of `compare_sources`.
  Mutations: the last partial chunk not visited; values returned in completion order.
- A12.2 **The hex document (D-326) [W12a].** `core/hikasa-hex/tests/document.rs`: reads at every page edge and across
  pages equal the file bytes; the LRU holds at most `cache_pages` pages (counting allocator: ≤ 16 MiB + 1 KiB after
  reading a 64 MiB file twice at random); a file ≤ `unlocked_max` is `Memory` and its handle is closed (Windows: the file
  can be replaced while the document is open; Linux: the inode is not held — `/proc/self/fd` has no entry), a larger one
  is `File`; an archive member is `TempCache` and reads equal `vfs cat`; stdin and clipboard blobs are `Memory`; a
  truncation is `Truncated`, a changed mtime gives `input_changed` through `check_unchanged`. Mutation: an eviction that
  serves the evicted page's bytes for its successor.
- A12.3 **None alignment and sections (D-327, D-328) [W12a].** `tests/align_none.rs`: goldens (compact text dumps,
  `tests/fixtures/golden/*.txt`) of equal files, a one-byte change, runs 7 and 8 equal bytes apart (merge vs not), a
  longer right file (tail `right_only`), empty files; P-NONE — the sections and statistics equal a naive byte loop's for
  random pairs with planted runs across chunk edges; with `max_sections` lowered to 4, `sections_truncated` and exact
  statistics; the thumbnail's buckets sum to the statistics. Mutations: the merge gap off by one; a run spanning a chunk
  edge counted twice.
- A12.4 **Fast alignment (D-329) [W12a].** `tests/align_fast.rs`: `GEAR` pinned (CRC of the table); chunk cuts identical
  across threads and visits; after an insertion of 1 byte, 1 KiB and 1 MiB at the start, middle and end, the blocks
  resynchronize within one block (golden segment lists); a moved block, a deletion, a replacement; P-HEXALIGN for every
  mode — segments cover each file exactly once in order, `Paired` segments have equal lengths, statistics equal a byte
  count over the segments, `compare(a, a)` is one `Paired` segment, swapping sides swaps `LeftOnly`/`RightOnly` and the
  statistics; peak live heap of a 64 MiB pair (counting allocator) within the §1.12.6 bound. Mutations: a cut that
  ignores the minimum length; the segment end not forced (chunking depends on threads).
- A12.5 **Complete alignment (D-330) [W12a].** `tests/align_complete.rs`: a 1-byte insertion inside a block that Fast
  pairs as changed is a 1-byte `RightOnly` under Complete; on random pairs ≤ 4 KiB with up to 8 edits Complete's
  non-same columns ≤ Fast's ≤ None's (and Complete's equal a reference LCS cost within Myers' heuristic bound on inputs
  of ≤ 256 bytes); a gap larger than the window walks with the `W/2` rule (golden); an unrelated gap is laid out
  None-style; a budget of 1 MiB degrades the same gaps with 1 and 16 threads and warns `alignment_degraded`.
  Mutation: the walk commits past `W/2`; the budget charged in completion order.
- A12.6 **Verdict (D-331) [W12a].** Table test of every row of §1.12.8 (the conversion rows with a fake converter on
  `MemoryVfs`); no mode ever answers 12. Mutation: Fast's verdict taken from block hashes (a planted collision pair
  must still be `binary_different`).
- A12.7 **Rows, layout, filters (D-332) [W12a].** `tests/rows.rs`: rows for bytes per line 1, 7, 16, 256, groups 1–8,

  with context 0 and 3 and their `hidden_before` counts; P-HEXROWS — `row_of(side, offset)` and the row's address round

### 6.13 W13 acceptance

Rules for every item: those of §6.4 (window tests and measurements only under `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY xvfb-run -a`;
everything else headless through the models), §6.6 (platforms, times, no timers, faults, gates), §6.7 and §6.8 (tests
can fail, goldens, help and text), §6.9's and §6.11's *through the models* and *exactness* rules, §6.12's *headless
inputs* rule, and:

- **Through the models.** GUI tests build `AppCore` over a temporary configuration (fixed clock and zone,
  `FixedClipboard` with images, `RecordingLauncher`, a private IPC endpoint, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` fixed for reports) and
  inputs generated by the test (seeded xorshift byte files with planted runs and edits; pictures built in memory and
  written as PNM by a small in-test writer or as PNG through `hikasa_session::clipboard::encode_png_rgba` — the GUI's
  sources, tests included, never name `image`, D-373); they drive `execute(window, Invocation)`, the panes' key and
  pointer calls with `FixedMetrics` and fixed pane rectangles, dialog models and `poll()`; jobs are awaited by polling
  (bounded) and held by gates where a test needs one in flight (an alignment, a prefetch, a geometry job, a tile batch,
  a report, a quick compare). Frame times are explicit (`now` arguments). Texture uploads are recorded by a fake texture
  sink of the model (the `ui/` owner is exercised by the optional window test only).
- **Exactness.** Wherever the window's result must equal core's or the CLI's (the landed alignment and `hex compare
  --json`; a find hit and `HexFinder::next`; the value panel and `hex dump --values`; the picture statistics after a drag,
  a nudge, a transform or a tolerance change and `picture compare … --json`; a tile drawn and `render_tile`; a report from
  the dialog and the CLI shortcut's bytes; the Quick Compare result and `hikasa quick`; a tab's write and `session edit
  --set`), the test compares the complete results.
- **Tests can fail.** Each property test of W13 (P-HEXSCREEN, P-HEXCARET, P-VIEWPORT, P-TILESCREEN, P-PICJOBS,
  P-REPORTVOCAB, P-TABS-ID for the new tabs) and each integration test that stands in for one (A13.1, A13.5, A13.13,
  A13.17, A13.20) is checked by mutation (docs/17 §3 point 6): the mutations named below are the minimum; §1.13.26 lists
  each, the test that caught it and the seed where there is one.

**Where each runs**

| Test | Linux CI | Windows CI | macOS CI | wine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| core additions (A13.2 `try_rows`, A13.4 `copy`, A13.8 `format_with`, A13.11 `parse_zoom`, A13.16, A13.19's two calls, A13.21's inference) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| GUI models (A13.1…A13.8, A13.10…A13.14, A13.17…A13.23) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| clipboard images (A13.14) | `FixedClipboard`; arboard by hand | `FixedClipboard` | `FixedClipboard` | `FixedClipboard` |
| watch, reload, changes on disk (A13.5) | disk | disk | disk (APFS) | disk |
| window test (A13.24, optional) | `xvfb-run`, `#[ignore]` | — | — | — |
| G10/G11 GUI rows, ARCH-GUI-003 (A13.9, A13.15, A13.26) | by hand, `#[ignore]`, llvmpipe | — | — | — |
| full screen, real clipboards, real GPU (A13.29) | maintainer's desktop | maintainer | maintainer | — |

  pointer under it after each wheel step (within 1e-9), keep the three panes' centres on one area point, and keep 32
  points of the area in every pane; the pan rules per button and pane; full screen enters and leaves with the previous
